segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज के शब्द

segments.src: - **Secondary data** — information collected by someone else for another purpose (Census tables, trade reports, your own past sales); cheap and fast, but rarely a perfect fit for your question.
segments.tr: - **माध्यमिक डेटा** — किसी और द्वारा किसी अन्य उद्देश्य के लिए एकत्र की गई जानकारी (जनगणना तालिकाएं, व्यापार रिपोर्ट, अपनी पिछली बिक्री); सस्ता और तेज़, लेकिन शायद ही कभी आपके प्रश्न के लिए एक परिपूर्ण फिट।

segments.src: - **Probability sample** — a sample in which every member of the sampling frame has a known, non-zero chance of being selected; the precondition that makes margin of error meaningful.
segments.tr: - **संभाव्यता नमूना** — एक नमूना जिसमें नमूना फ्रेम का हर सदस्य चयन की ज्ञात, गैर-शून्य संभावना रखता है; वह पूर्वशर्त जो त्रुटि के मार्जिन को सार्थक बनाता है।

segments.src: - **Non-response bias** — distortion that occurs when the people who don't answer differ systematically from those who do; more responses don't fix it.
segments.tr: - **गैर-प्रतिक्रिया पूर्वाग्रह** — विकृति जो तब होती है जब जो लोग उत्तर नहीं देते हैं वे उन लोगों से व्यवस्थित रूप से भिन्न होते हैं जो करते हैं; अधिक प्रतिक्रियाएं इसे ठीक नहीं करती हैं।

segments.src: - **Consideration set** — the small handful of brands a buyer actually weighs at the evaluation stage; being known but not in the set is a distinct problem from being unknown.
segments.tr: - **विचार सेट** — ब्रांड की छोटी मुट्ठी भर जो एक खरीदार मूल्यांकन चरण में वजन करता है; ज्ञात लेकिन सेट में न होना अज्ञात होने से एक अलग समस्या है।

segments.src: - **Post-purchase dissonance** — the doubt a buyer feels after committing, especially on high-involvement purchases; managing it drives returns, reviews, and repeat business.
segments.tr: - **क्रय-पश्चात असहमति** — संदेह जो एक खरीदार प्रतिबद्ध होने के बाद महसूस करता है, विशेष रूप से उच्च-संलग्नता खरीद पर; इसे प्रबंधित करना रिटर्न, समीक्षाएं, और दोहराई गई व्यवसाय चलाती है।

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Only a controlled experiment separates "the coupon caused the reorder" from "reorder-prone customers redeem coupons."
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **1 — C।** केवल एक नियंत्रित प्रयोग "कूपन ने पुनः ऑर्डर का कारण बना" को "पुनः ऑर्डर करने वाले ग्राहकों ने कूपन भुनाया" से अलग करता है।

segments.src: A survey measures opinion about coupons, not their effect.
segments.tr: एक सर्वेक्षण कूपन के बारे में राय को मापता है, उनके प्रभाव को नहीं।

segments.src: **2 — False.** It's double-barreled ("fast" and "easy" are two questions with possibly opposite answers) and leading.
segments.tr: **2 — गलत।** यह दोहरा-बैरेल्ड है ("तेज़" और "आसान" संभवतः विपरीत उत्तरों के साथ दो प्रश्न हैं) और नेतृत्व करता है।

segments.src: Split it into two neutral items.
segments.tr: इसे दो तटस्थ वस्तुओं में विभाजित करें।

segments.src: **3 — D.** Rereading reviews after paying is post-purchase dissonance, not information search — the search is over; she's now reducing doubt about a decision already made.*
segments.tr: **3 — D।** भुगतान के बाद समीक्षाओं को दोबारा पढ़ना क्रय-पश्चात असहमति है, सूचना खोज नहीं — खोज समाप्त है; वह अब एक निर्णय के बारे में संदेह को कम कर रही है जो पहले से ही किया गया है।*

es.title: [Marketing 101 #3] Las personas no mienten en encuestas — simplemente no saben por qué compran

segments.src: > Good market research isn't about asking customers what they want; it's about designing a question honest enough that the answer means something — then reading it against how people actually decide.
segments.tr: > Una buena investigación de mercado no se trata de preguntar a los clientes qué quieren; se trata de diseñar una pregunta lo suficientemente honesta para que la respuesta signifique algo — y luego interpretarla según cómo las personas realmente deciden.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: This lesson has two halves that only work when you put them together.
segments.tr: Esta lección tiene dos mitades que solo funcionan cuando las juntas.

segments.src: **Half one: research design.** Marketing research is a process, not a survey link.
segments.tr: **Primera mitad: diseño de investigación.** La investigación de marketing es un proceso, no un enlace de encuesta.

segments.src: It runs: define the decision you need to make → choose a design → collect data → analyze → act.
segments.tr: Se ejecuta así: define la decisión que necesitas tomar → elige un diseño → recopila datos → analiza → actúa.

segments.src: Skipping straight to "let's send out a survey" is the single most common way companies buy expensive noise.
segments.tr: Saltarse directamente a "enviemos una encuesta" es la forma más común en que las empresas compran ruido costoso.

segments.src: Start with **secondary data** — information someone already collected.
segments.tr: Comienza con **datos secundarios** — información que alguien ya recopiló.

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: EE.UU.

segments.src: Census and Bureau of Labor Statistics tables, trade association reports, Google Trends, and above all your own sales and support logs.
segments.tr: Tablas del Censo y de la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales, informes de asociaciones comerciales, Google Trends, y sobre todo tus propios registros de ventas y soporte.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast, but it was gathered for someone else's question, so it rarely answers yours exactly.
segments.tr: Es barato y rápido, pero fue recopilado para la pregunta de otra persona, así que rara vez responde exactamente la tuya.

segments.src: When you need **primary data** — data you collect yourself — pick the design that matches what you don't know:
segments.tr: Cuando necesites **datos primarios** — datos que recopiles tú mismo — elige el diseño que coincida con lo que no sabes:

segments.src: - **Exploratory** — "What's even going on here?" In-depth interviews, focus groups, open-ended questions. Output is hypotheses, not numbers.
segments.tr: - **Exploratorio** — "¿Qué está pasando aquí?" Entrevistas en profundidad, grupos focales, preguntas abiertas. El resultado son hipótesis, no números.

segments.src: - **Descriptive** — "How many, how often, who?" Surveys, panels, observation. Output is a measurement.
segments.tr: - **Descriptivo** — "¿Cuántos, con qué frecuencia, quién?" Encuestas, paneles, observación. El resultado es una medición.

segments.src: - **Causal** — "Does X actually cause Y?" Controlled experiments and A/B tests, where you change one thing and hold the rest steady.
segments.tr: - **Causal** — "¿Realmente X causa Y?" Experimentos controlados y pruebas A/B, donde cambias una cosa y mantienes el resto constante.

segments.src: The classic blunder is running a descriptive survey before you've done any exploratory work — you end up precisely measuring the wrong thing.
segments.tr: El error clásico es ejecutar una encuesta descriptiva antes de haber hecho ningún trabajo exploratorio — acabas midiendo con precisión la cosa equivocada.

segments.src: **Survey craft, briefly.** Two things decide whether a survey is worth reading:
segments.tr: **Redacción de encuestas, en breve.** Dos cosas decidirán si una encuesta vale la pena leer:

segments.src: 1. *Who answered.* Your **sampling frame** is the list you drew from; a **probability sample** gives everyone in that frame a known chance of selection, which is what makes margin of error meaningful. A convenience sample — your Instagram followers, people who clicked the email — doesn't. Sample size matters less than most people think, and depends barely at all on population size: roughly `n = 1,000 → about ±3 percentage points` at 95% confidence, whether you're describing Rhode Island or the entire country. **Non-response bias** is the bigger threat: if only your happiest and angriest customers reply, more responses just make a skewed picture look confident.
segments.tr: 1. *Quién respondió.* Tu **marco de muestreo** es la lista de la que extrajiste; una **muestra de probabilidad** le da a todos en ese marco una oportunidad conocida de selección, lo que hace que el margen de error sea significativo. Una muestra de conveniencia — tus seguidores de Instagram, personas que hicieron clic en el correo — no lo hace. El tamaño de la muestra importa menos de lo que la mayoría piensa, y depende apenas nada del tamaño de la población: aproximadamente `n = 1,000 → alrededor de ±3 puntos porcentuales` con 95% de confianza, ya sea que estés describiendo Rhode Island o todo el país. **El sesgo de no respuesta** es la amenaza mayor: si solo tus clientes más felices y más enojados responden, más respuestas solo hacen que una imagen sesgada se vea confiada.

segments.src: 2. *What you asked.* Watch for **leading** questions ("How much did you enjoy our new checkout?"), **double-barreled** ones ("Is our checkout fast and easy?" — which half are you answering?), and **social desirability bias**, where people report the flattering answer. Then there's the **say-do gap**: stated purchase intent reliably overstates real purchasing, especially about price and about virtuous behavior. "Would you pay $30 a month for this?" is nearly worthless. "What are you paying today, and what did you do the last time you needed this?" is not.
segments.tr: 2. *Lo que preguntaste.* Ten cuidado con preguntas **sesgadas** ("¿Cuánto disfrutaste de nuestro nuevo checkout?"), **dobles** ("¿Nuestro checkout es rápido y fácil?" — ¿cuál mitad estás respondiendo?), y **sesgo de deseabilidad social**, donde las personas reportan la respuesta halagadora. Luego está el **sesgo entre decir y hacer**: la intención de compra declarada sobrestima sistemáticamente las compras reales, especialmente sobre precio y comportamiento virtuoso. "¿Pagarías $30 al mes por esto?" es casi inútil. "¿Cuánto estás pagando hoy, y qué hiciste la última vez que necesitabas esto?" no lo es.

segments.src: **Half two: how buyers actually decide.** The standard model has five stages:
segments.tr: **Segunda mitad: cómo los compradores realmente deciden.** El modelo estándar tiene cinco etapas:

segments.src: 1. **Problem recognition** — a gap opens between where you are and where you want to be.
segments.tr: 1. **Reconocimiento del problema** — se abre una brecha entre dónde estás y dónde quieres estar.

segments.src: 2. **Information search** — internal (memory) first, then external (reviews, friends, retail floors).
segments.tr: 2. **Búsqueda de información** — interna (memoria) primero, luego externa (reseñas, amigos, pisos de retail).

segments.src: 3. **Evaluation of alternatives** — a short **consideration set** gets scored on a handful of **evaluative criteria**.
segments.tr: 3. **Evaluación de alternativas** — un **conjunto de consideración** corto se califica en un puñado de **criterios de evaluación**.

segments.src: 4. **Purchase decision** — plus the last-second friction that kills it: shipping cost, out of stock, a bad checkout.
segments.tr: 4. **Decisión de compra** — más la fricción del último segundo que la mata: costo de envío, agotado, un mal checkout.

segments.src: 5. **Post-purchase behavior** — satisfaction, **post-purchase dissonance** (buyer's remorse), returns, reviews, repeat business.
segments.tr: 5. **Comportamiento post-compra** — satisfacción, **disonancia post-compra** (arrepentimiento del comprador), devoluciones, reseñas, negocios repetidos.

segments.src: Not every purchase runs the full loop.
segments.tr: No todas las compras corren el ciclo completo.

segments.src: **High-involvement** buys — expensive, risky, identity-relevant — get the extended treatment.
segments.tr: Las compras **de alto involucramiento** — costosas, riesgosas, relevantes para la identidad — reciben el tratamiento extendido.

segments.src: Low-involvement ones (toothpaste, gas station coffee) are mostly habit, which is why for those categories the real battleground is availability and cue, not persuasion.
segments.tr: Las de bajo involucramiento (pasta de dientes, café de gasolinera) son en su mayoría hábito, por eso en esas categorías el verdadero campo de batalla es disponibilidad y señal, no persuasión.

segments.src: Put the halves together and you get the useful rule: **choose your research design based on the stage where you're losing people.**
segments.tr: Junta las dos mitades y obtienes la regla útil: **elige tu diseño de investigación basado en la etapa donde estás perdiendo gente.**

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Maya moves into a one-bedroom in Denver and, on night three, wakes up with her lower back aching.
segments.tr: Maya se muda a un apartamento de una habitación en Denver y, en la noche tres, se despierta con dolor de espalda baja.

segments.src: That's **problem recognition** — nothing about her mattress changed, but her tolerance did.
segments.tr: Eso es **reconocimiento del problema** — nada sobre su colchón cambió, pero su tolerancia sí.

segments.src: **Information search:** she texts two friends, reads a "best mattress 2026" roundup, watches a YouTube teardown, and — because she's spending real money — drives to a store on Colorado Boulevard to lie on three of them for ninety seconds each.
segments.tr: **Búsqueda de información:** envía mensajes de texto a dos amigos, lee un resumen de "mejor colchón 2026", ve un desmontaje en YouTube, y — porque está gastando dinero real — maneja a una tienda en Colorado Boulevard para acostarse en tres de ellos noventa segundos cada uno.

segments.src: **Evaluation of alternatives:** her **consideration set** narrows to three brands.
segments.tr: **Evaluación de alternativas:** su **conjunto de consideración** se reduce a tres marcas.

segments.src: Her **evaluative criteria** turn out to be firmness, a sleep trial she can actually use, and price under about $1,500.
segments.tr: Sus **criterios de evaluación** resultan ser firmeza, una prueba de sueño que pueda usar, y precio bajo alrededor de $1,500.

segments.src: Note that "made in the USA" was in the ad that got her attention but never made her criteria list — attention and criteria are different things.
segments.tr: Ten en cuenta que "hecho en EE.UU." estaba en el anuncio que llamó su atención pero nunca entró en su lista de criterios — atención y criterios son cosas diferentes.

segments.src: **Purchase decision:** she picks a $1,400 queen at 11 p.m., then almost bails when old-mattress removal costs $99 extra.
segments.tr: **Decisión de compra:** elige una queen de $1,400 a las 11 p.m., luego casi se retira cuando la remoción del colchón viejo cuesta $99 extra.

segments.src: Free removal in the cart is what closes it.
segments.tr: La remoción gratuita en el carrito es lo que la cierra.

segments.src: **Post-purchase:** week one is rough.
segments.tr: **Post-compra:** la primera semana es difícil.

segments.src: She rereads the reviews she already read, looking for someone saying "it takes two weeks to adjust."
segments.tr: Relee las reseñas que ya leyó, buscando a alguien que diga "toma dos semanas adaptarse."

segments.src: That's **post-purchase dissonance**, and it's the moment brands either earn a five-star review or a return.
segments.tr: Eso es **disonancia post-compra**, y es el momento en que las marcas se ganan una reseña de cinco estrellas o una devolución.

segments.src: Now flip to the mattress company's side.
segments.tr: Ahora cambia al lado de la empresa de colchones.

segments.src: If Maya's story is typical, the research plan writes itself, stage by stage:
segments.tr: Si la historia de Maya es típica, el plan de investigación se escribe a sí mismo, etapa por etapa:

segments.src: - Suspect people don't know what firmness they need? That's fuzzy — run **exploratory** interviews with recent buyers.
segments.tr: - ¿Sospechas que las personas no saben qué firmeza necesitan? Eso es vago — ejecuta entrevistas **exploratorias** con compradores recientes.

segments.src: - Want to know what share of buyers rank a sleep trial above price? That's a count — run a **descriptive** survey on a probability sample of the customer list, and chase non-responders so it isn't just the enthusiasts.
segments.tr: - ¿Quieres saber qué proporción de compradores clasifican una prueba de sueño por encima del precio? Eso es un conteo — ejecuta una encuesta **descriptiva** en una muestra de probabilidad de la lista de clientes, y persigue a los no respondedores para que no sean solo los entusiastas.

segments.src: - Think free removal lifts conversion? Don't survey it — people are terrible at reporting what a $99 fee does to them. Run a **causal** A/B test at checkout and watch behavior.
segments.tr: - ¿Crees que la remoción gratuita aumenta la conversión? No lo encuestes — las personas son terribles reportando lo que una tarifa de $99 les hace. Ejecuta una prueba A/B **causal** en el checkout y observa el comportamiento.

segments.src: - Worried about returns in week two? That's a post-purchase problem, and the fix is probably an email on day 5 explaining the adjustment period, not a better ad.
segments.tr: - ¿Preocupado por devoluciones en la segunda semana? Eso es un problema post-compra, y la solución probablemente es un correo en el día 5 explicando el período de ajuste, no un mejor anuncio.

segments.src: Same company, four questions, four different designs.
segments.tr: La misma empresa, cuatro preguntas, cuatro diseños diferentes.

segments.src: A single "customer satisfaction survey" would have answered none of them well.
segments.tr: Una única "encuesta de satisfacción del cliente" no habría respondido bien a ninguna de ellas.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Match the design to the question: exploratory to find hypotheses, descriptive to measure them, causal to prove what drives what — and check secondary data before you spend a dollar on primary.
segments.tr: 1. Empareja el diseño con la pregunta: exploratorio para encontrar hipótesis, descriptivo para medirlas, causal para probar qué impulsa qué — y verifica datos secundarios antes de gastar un dólar en primarios.

segments.src: 2. A survey is only as good as who answered and how you asked; non-response bias, leading or double-barreled wording, and the say-do gap ruin more studies than small sample sizes do.
segments.tr: 2. Una encuesta es tan buena como quién respondió y cómo preguntaste; el sesgo de no respuesta, la redacción sesgada o doble, y el sesgo entre decir y hacer arruinan más estudios que los tamaños de muestra pequeños.

segments.src: 3. Buyers move through problem recognition → search → evaluation → purchase → post-purchase, and the stage where you're losing them tells you which research to run.
segments.tr: 3. Los compradores se mueven a través de reconocimiento del problema → búsqueda → evaluación → compra → post-compra, y la etapa donde los estás perdiendo te dice qué investigación ejecutar.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: **1.** A direct-to-consumer coffee brand wants to know whether a $5-off coupon actually causes repeat orders, or whether the people who redeem it would have reordered anyway.
segments.tr: **1.** Una marca de café directo al consumidor quiere saber si un cupón de descuento de $5 realmente causa pedidos repetidos, o si las personas que lo canjean hubieran hecho reorden de todos modos.

segments.src: Which research design fits?
segments.tr: ¿Qué diseño de investigación se ajusta?

segments.src: - A. Exploratory — run two focus groups about coupons
segments.tr: - A. Exploratorio — ejecuta dos grupos focales sobre cupones

segments.src: - B. Descriptive — survey customers on how much they like coupons
segments.tr: - B. Descriptivo — encuesta a los clientes sobre cuánto les gustan los cupones

segments.src: - C. Causal — randomly give the coupon to one group, withhold it from a comparable group, compare reorder rates
segments.tr: - C. Causal — da aleatoriamente el cupón a un grupo, retíralo a un grupo comparable, compara tasas de reorden

segments.src: - D. Secondary — buy an industry report on coupon usage
segments.tr: - D. Secundario — compra un informe de la industria sobre uso de cupones

segments.src: **2.** True or False: "Is our checkout fast and easy?"
segments.tr: **2.** Verdadero o Falso: "¿Nuestro checkout es rápido y fácil?"

segments.src: is a well-written survey question.
segments.tr: es una pregunta de encuesta bien redactada.

segments.src: **3.** A shopper who has already paid $1,400 keeps rereading reviews to reassure herself she chose right.
segments.tr: **3.** Una compradora que ya pagó $1,400 sigue releyendo reseñas para asegurarse de que eligió bien.

segments.src: Which stage is this?
segments.tr: ¿Cuál es esta etapa?

segments.src: - A. Problem recognition
segments.tr: - A. Reconocimiento del problema

segments.src: - B. Information search
segments.tr: - B. Búsqueda de información

segments.src: - C. Purchase decision
segments.tr: - C. Decisión de compra

segments.src: - D. Post-purchase behavior
segments.tr: - D. Comportamiento post-compra

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Secondary data** — information collected by someone else for another purpose (Census tables, trade reports, your own past sales); cheap and fast, but rarely a perfect fit for your question.
segments.tr: - **Datos secundarios** — información recopilada por otro para otro propósito (tablas del censo, informes comerciales, tus propias ventas pasadas); barato y rápido, pero rara vez se ajusta perfectamente a tu pregunta.

segments.src: - **Probability sample** — a sample in which every member of the sampling frame has a known, non-zero chance of being selected; the precondition that makes margin of error meaningful.
segments.tr: - **Muestra de probabilidad** — una muestra en la que cada miembro del marco de muestreo tiene una oportunidad conocida, diferente de cero, de ser seleccionado; la precondición que hace que el margen de error sea significativo.

segments.src: - **Non-response bias** — distortion that occurs when the people who don't answer differ systematically from those who do; more responses don't fix it.
segments.tr: - **Sesgo de no respuesta** — distorsión que ocurre cuando las personas que no responden difieren sistemáticamente de las que sí; más respuestas no lo arreglan.

segments.src: - **Consideration set** — the small handful of brands a buyer actually weighs at the evaluation stage; being known but not in the set is a distinct problem from being unknown.
segments.tr: - **Conjunto de consideración** — el pequeño puñado de marcas que un comprador realmente pesa en la etapa de evaluación; ser conocido pero no en el conjunto es un problema distinto de ser desconocido.

segments.src: - **Post-purchase dissonance** — the doubt a buyer feels after committing, especially on high-involvement purchases; managing it drives returns, reviews, and repeat business.
segments.tr: - **Disonancia post-compra** — la duda que siente un comprador después de comprometerse, especialmente en compras de alto involucramiento; gestionarla impulsa devoluciones, reseñas y negocios repetidos.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Only a controlled experiment separates "the coupon caused the reorder" from "reorder-prone customers redeem coupons."
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **1 — C.** Solo un experimento controlado separa "el cupón causó el reorden" de "los clientes propensos a reordenar canjean cupones."

segments.src: A survey measures opinion about coupons, not their effect.
segments.tr: Una encuesta mide la opinión sobre cupones, no su efecto.

segments.src: **2 — False.** It's double-barreled ("fast" and "easy" are two questions with possibly opposite answers) and leading.
segments.tr: **2 — Falso.** Es doble ("rápido" y "fácil" son dos preguntas con posibles respuestas opuestas) y sesgado.

segments.src: Split it into two neutral items.
segments.tr: Divídelo en dos elementos neutrales.

segments.src: **3 — D.** Rereading reviews after paying is post-purchase dissonance, not information search — the search is over; she's now reducing doubt about a decision already made.*
segments.tr: **3 — D.** Releer reseñas después de pagar es disonancia post-compra, no búsqueda de información — la búsqueda terminó; ahora está reduciendo la duda sobre una decisión ya tomada.*

ar.title: [Marketing 101 #3] الناس لا يكذبون في الاستطلاعات — فقط لا يعرفون لماذا يشترون

segments.src: > Good market research isn't about asking customers what they want; it's about designing a question honest enough that the answer means something — then reading it against how people actually decide.
segments.tr: > البحث السوقي الجيد لا يتعلق بسؤال العملاء عما يريدونه؛ بل يتعلق بتصميم سؤال صادق بما يكفي بحيث تكون الإجابة ذات معنى — ثم قراءتها مقابل كيفية اتخاذ الناس القرارات فعلياً.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: This lesson has two halves that only work when you put them together.
segments.tr: لهذا الدرس جزءان يعملان فقط عندما تجمعهما معاً.

segments.src: **Half one: research design.** Marketing research is a process, not a survey link.
segments.tr: **الجزء الأول: تصميم البحث.** البحث التسويقي هو عملية، وليس رابط استطلاع.

segments.src: It runs: define the decision you need to make → choose a design → collect data → analyze → act.
segments.tr: يعمل كالتالي: حدد القرار الذي تحتاج إلى اتخاذه → اختر تصميماً → اجمع البيانات → حلل → تصرف.

segments.src: Skipping straight to "let's send out a survey" is the single most common way companies buy expensive noise.
segments.tr: تخطي الخطوات والذهاب مباشرة إلى "دعنا نرسل استطلاعاً" هو الطريقة الأكثر شيوعاً التي تشتري بها الشركات ضوضاء مكلفة.

segments.src: Start with **secondary data** — information someone already collected.
segments.tr: ابدأ ببيانات **ثانوية** — معلومات جمعها شخص آخر بالفعل.

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: U.S.

segments.src: Census and Bureau of Labor Statistics tables, trade association reports, Google Trends, and above all your own sales and support logs.
segments.tr: جداول الإحصاء السكاني وجداول مكتب إحصائيات العمل، تقارير جمعيات التجارة، Google Trends، والأهم من ذلك سجلات المبيعات والدعم الخاصة بك.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast, but it was gathered for someone else's question, so it rarely answers yours exactly.
segments.tr: إنها رخيصة وسريعة، لكن تم جمعها للإجابة على سؤال شخص آخر، لذا نادراً ما تجيب على سؤالك بالضبط.

segments.src: When you need **primary data** — data you collect yourself — pick the design that matches what you don't know:
segments.tr: عندما تحتاج إلى بيانات **أولية** — البيانات التي تجمعها بنفسك — اختر التصميم الذي يطابق ما لا تعرفه:

segments.src: - **Exploratory** — "What's even going on here?" In-depth interviews, focus groups, open-ended questions. Output is hypotheses, not numbers.
segments.tr: - **استكشافي** — "ما الذي يحدث هنا؟" مقابلات متعمقة، مجموعات تركيز، أسئلة مفتوحة النهاية. المخرجات هي فرضيات، وليست أرقام.

segments.src: - **Descriptive** — "How many, how often, who?" Surveys, panels, observation. Output is a measurement.
segments.tr: - **وصفي** — "كم عدد، كم مرة، من؟" الاستطلاعات، الألواح، الملاحظة. المخرجات هي قياس.

segments.src: - **Causal** — "Does X actually cause Y?" Controlled experiments and A/B tests, where you change one thing and hold the rest steady.
segments.tr: - **سببي** — "هل X يسبب فعلاً Y؟" التجارب المراقبة واختبارات A/B، حيث تغير شيء واحد وتحافظ على الباقي ثابتاً.

segments.src: The classic blunder is running a descriptive survey before you've done any exploratory work — you end up precisely measuring the wrong thing.
segments.tr: الخطأ الكلاسيكي هو إجراء استطلاع وصفي قبل القيام بأي عمل استكشافي — ينتهي بك الحال إلى قياس الشيء الخاطئ بدقة.

segments.src: **Survey craft, briefly.** Two things decide whether a survey is worth reading:
segments.tr: **صياغة الاستطلاع، باختصار.** شيئان يحددان ما إذا كان الاستطلاع يستحق القراءة:

segments.src: 1. *Who answered.* Your **sampling frame** is the list you drew from; a **probability sample** gives everyone in that frame a known chance of selection, which is what makes margin of error meaningful. A convenience sample — your Instagram followers, people who clicked the email — doesn't. Sample size matters less than most people think, and depends barely at all on population size: roughly `n = 1,000 → about ±3 percentage points` at 95% confidence, whether you're describing Rhode Island or the entire country. **Non-response bias** is the bigger threat: if only your happiest and angriest customers reply, more responses just make a skewed picture look confident.
segments.tr: 1. *من أجاب.* **إطار العينة** الخاص بك هو القائمة التي استخرجت منها؛ **عينة احتمالية** تعطي كل شخص في هذا الإطار فرصة معروفة للاختيار، وهذا هو ما يجعل هامش الخطأ ذا معنى. عينة مريحة — متابعوك على Instagram، الأشخاص الذين نقروا على البريد الإلكتروني — لا تفعل. حجم العينة مهم أقل مما يعتقده معظم الناس، ويعتمد بالكاد على حجم السكان: تقريباً `n = 1,000 → حوالي ±3 نقاط مئوية` بثقة 95%، سواء كنت تصف Rhode Island أو البلد بأكملها. **التحيز عدم الاستجابة** هو التهديد الأكبر: إذا أجاب فقط عملاؤك الأكثر سعادة وغضباً، فإن المزيد من الاستجابات تجعل الصورة المنحرفة تبدو واثقة.

segments.src: 2. *What you asked.* Watch for **leading** questions ("How much did you enjoy our new checkout?"), **double-barreled** ones ("Is our checkout fast and easy?" — which half are you answering?), and **social desirability bias**, where people report the flattering answer. Then there's the **say-do gap**: stated purchase intent reliably overstates real purchasing, especially about price and about virtuous behavior. "Would you pay $30 a month for this?" is nearly worthless. "What are you paying today, and what did you do the last time you needed this?" is not.
segments.tr: 2. *ما الذي سألت عنه.* انتبه إلى الأسئلة **الموجهة** ("ما مدى استمتاعك باستخراج الخروج الجديد لدينا؟")، **مزدوج البرميل** ("هل استخراج الخروج لدينا سريع وسهل؟" — أي نصف تجيب عليه؟)، و**التحيز بالرغبة الاجتماعية**، حيث يبلغ الناس عن الإجابة المتملقة. ثم هناك **الفجوة بين القول والفعل**: النية المعلنة للشراء تبالغ بشكل موثوق في الشراء الفعلي، خاصة بشأن السعر وحول السلوك الفاضل. "هل ستدفع $30 شهرياً لهذا؟" بلا قيمة تقريباً. "ما الذي تدفعه اليوم، وماذا فعلت آخر مرة احتجت فيها لهذا؟" لا يفعل.

segments.src: **Half two: how buyers actually decide.** The standard model has five stages:
segments.tr: **الجزء الثاني: كيف يقرر المشترون فعلاً.** النموذج القياسي له خمس مراحل:

segments.src: 1. **Problem recognition** — a gap opens between where you are and where you want to be.
segments.tr: 1. **الاعتراف بالمشكلة** — تنفتح فجوة بين حيث أنت وحيث تريد أن تكون.

segments.src: 2. **Information search** — internal (memory) first, then external (reviews, friends, retail floors).
segments.tr: 2. **البحث عن المعلومات** — داخلي (الذاكرة) أولاً، ثم خارجي (المراجعات، الأصدقاء، أرضيات البيع بالتجزئة).

segments.src: 3. **Evaluation of alternatives** — a short **consideration set** gets scored on a handful of **evaluative criteria**.
segments.tr: 3. **تقييم البدائل** — يتم تسجيل **مجموعة الاعتبار** القصيرة على عدد قليل من **معايير التقييم**.

segments.src: 4. **Purchase decision** — plus the last-second friction that kills it: shipping cost, out of stock, a bad checkout.
segments.tr: 4. **قرار الشراء** — بالإضافة إلى الاحتكاك اللحظة الأخيرة الذي يقتله: تكلفة الشحن، غير متوفر، استخراج خروج سيء.

segments.src: 5. **Post-purchase behavior** — satisfaction, **post-purchase dissonance** (buyer's remorse), returns, reviews, repeat business.
segments.tr: 5. **السلوك بعد الشراء** — الرضا، **الفجوة بعد الشراء** (ندم المشتري)، الإرجاعات، المراجعات، تكرار الأعمال.

segments.src: Not every purchase runs the full loop.
segments.tr: لا يمر كل شراء بالحلقة كاملة.

segments.src: **High-involvement** buys — expensive, risky, identity-relevant — get the extended treatment.
segments.tr: المشتريات **عالية الانخراط** — مكلفة، محفوفة بالمخاطر، ذات صلة بالهوية — تحصل على المعاملة الموسعة.

segments.src: Low-involvement ones (toothpaste, gas station coffee) are mostly habit, which is why for those categories the real battleground is availability and cue, not persuasion.
segments.tr: المشتريات منخفضة الانخراط (معجون الأسنان، قهوة محطة الغاز) هي في الأساس عادة، وهذا هو السبب في أن ساحة المعركة الحقيقية لتلك الفئات هي التوفر والإشارة، وليس الإقناع.

segments.src: Put the halves together and you get the useful rule: **choose your research design based on the stage where you're losing people.**
segments.tr: ضع النصفين معاً وتحصل على القاعدة المفيدة: **اختر تصميم بحثك بناءً على المرحلة حيث تخسر الناس.**

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Maya moves into a one-bedroom in Denver and, on night three, wakes up with her lower back aching.
segments.tr: تنتقل مايا إلى شقة بغرفة نوم واحدة في Denver وفي الليلة الثالثة، تستيقظ وظهرها السفلي يؤلمها.

segments.src: That's **problem recognition** — nothing about her mattress changed, but her tolerance did.
segments.tr: هذا **الاعتراف بالمشكلة** — لم يتغير شيء حول مرتبتها، لكن تسامحها تغير.

segments.src: **Information search:** she texts two friends, reads a "best mattress 2026" roundup, watches a YouTube teardown, and — because she's spending real money — drives to a store on Colorado Boulevard to lie on three of them for ninety seconds each.
segments.tr: **البحث عن المعلومات:** ترسل رسالة نصية إلى صديقتين، تقرأ ملخص "أفضل مرتبة 2026"، تشاهد فيديو حول الفك، وتقود إلى متجر في طريق Colorado Boulevard للاستلقاء على ثلاثة منهم لمدة تسعين ثانية لكل منهما.

segments.src: **Evaluation of alternatives:** her **consideration set** narrows to three brands.
segments.tr: **تقييم البدائل:** تضيق **مجموعة الاعتبار** الخاصة بها إلى ثلاث علامات تجارية.

segments.src: Her **evaluative criteria** turn out to be firmness, a sleep trial she can actually use, and price under about $1,500.
segments.tr: اتضح أن **معايير التقييم** الخاصة بها هي الصلابة، تجربة نوم يمكنها فعلاً استخدامها، والسعر أقل من حوالي $1,500.

segments.src: Note that "made in the USA" was in the ad that got her attention but never made her criteria list — attention and criteria are different things.
segments.tr: لاحظ أن "مصنوع في USA" كان في الإعلان الذي لفت انتباهها لكنه لم يدخل أبداً قائمة معاييرها — الانتباه والمعايير أشياء مختلفة.

segments.src: **Purchase decision:** she picks a $1,400 queen at 11 p.m., then almost bails when old-mattress removal costs $99 extra.
segments.tr: **قرار الشراء:** تختار ملكة $1,400 في الساعة 11 p.m.، ثم تكاد تتراجع عندما تكلف إزالة المرتبة القديمة $99 إضافية.

segments.src: Free removal in the cart is what closes it.
segments.tr: الإزالة المجانية في السلة هي ما يغلقها.

segments.src: **Post-purchase:** week one is rough.
segments.tr: **بعد الشراء:** الأسبوع الأول صعب.

segments.src: She rereads the reviews she already read, looking for someone saying "it takes two weeks to adjust."
segments.tr: تقرأ المراجعات التي قرأتها بالفعل، باحثة عن شخص يقول "يستغرق أسبوعين للتعديل."

segments.src: That's **post-purchase dissonance**, and it's the moment brands either earn a five-star review or a return.
segments.tr: هذا **الفجوة بعد الشراء**، وهي اللحظة التي تكسب فيها العلامات التجارية إما مراجعة بخمس نجوم أو عودة.

segments.src: Now flip to the mattress company's side.
segments.tr: الآن انقلب إلى جانب شركة المرتبة.

segments.src: If Maya's story is typical, the research plan writes itself, stage by stage:
segments.tr: إذا كانت قصة مايا نموذجية، فإن خطة البحث تكتب نفسها بنفسها، مرحلة تلو الأخرى:

segments.src: - Suspect people don't know what firmness they need? That's fuzzy — run **exploratory** interviews with recent buyers.
segments.tr: - تشك في أن الناس لا يعرفون ما الصلابة التي يحتاجونها؟ هذا غير واضح — أجرِ مقابلات **استكشافية** مع المشترين الأخيرين.

segments.src: - Want to know what share of buyers rank a sleep trial above price? That's a count — run a **descriptive** survey on a probability sample of the customer list, and chase non-responders so it isn't just the enthusiasts.
segments.tr: - هل تريد أن تعرف ما نسبة المشترين الذين يصنفون تجربة النوم فوق السعر؟ هذا عد — أجرِ استطلاع **وصفي** على عينة احتمالية من قائمة العملاء، واتبع المستجيبين بشكل غير صحيح حتى لا يكون المتحمسون فقط.

segments.src: - Think free removal lifts conversion? Don't survey it — people are terrible at reporting what a $99 fee does to them. Run a **causal** A/B test at checkout and watch behavior.
segments.tr: - تعتقد أن الإزالة المجانية ترفع التحويل؟ لا تستطلعها — الناس سيئون في الإبلاغ عما تفعله رسوم $99. أجرِ اختبار A/B **سببي** عند الخروج ولاحظ السلوك.

segments.src: - Worried about returns in week two? That's a post-purchase problem, and the fix is probably an email on day 5 explaining the adjustment period, not a better ad.
segments.tr: - قلق بشأن الإرجاعات في الأسبوع الثاني؟ هذه مشكلة بعد الشراء، والحل هو ربما بريد إلكتروني في اليوم 5 يشرح فترة التعديل، وليس إعلان أفضل.

segments.src: Same company, four questions, four different designs.
segments.tr: نفس الشركة، أربعة أسئلة، أربعة تصاميم مختلفة.

segments.src: A single "customer satisfaction survey" would have answered none of them well.
segments.tr: لن يجيب "استطلاع رضا العملاء" الفردي على أي منهم بشكل جيد.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## ملخص ثلاث أسطر

segments.src: 1. Match the design to the question: exploratory to find hypotheses, descriptive to measure them, causal to prove what drives what — and check secondary data before you spend a dollar on primary.
segments.tr: 1. طابق التصميم مع السؤال: استكشافي للعثور على الفرضيات، وصفي لقياسها، سببي لإثبات ما يقود ماذا — وتحقق من البيانات الثانوية قبل أن تنفق دولاراً واحداً على البيانات الأولية.

segments.src: 2. A survey is only as good as who answered and how you asked; non-response bias, leading or double-barreled wording, and the say-do gap ruin more studies than small sample sizes do.
segments.tr: 2. الاستطلاع لا يكون جيداً إلا كم من أجاب وكيف سألت؛ تحيز عدم الاستجابة، الصياغة الموجهة أو مزدوجة البرميل، والفجوة بين القول والفعل تفسد المزيد من الدراسات أكثر من أحجام العينات الصغيرة.

segments.src: 3. Buyers move through problem recognition → search → evaluation → purchase → post-purchase, and the stage where you're losing them tells you which research to run.
segments.tr: 3. يتحرك المشترون عبر الاعتراف بالمشكلة → البحث → التقييم → الشراء → بعد الشراء، والمرحلة حيث تخسرهم تخبرك ببحث ما ستجري.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.src: **1.** A direct-to-consumer coffee brand wants to know whether a $5-off coupon actually causes repeat orders, or whether the people who redeem it would have reordered anyway.
segments.tr: **1.** تريد علامة تجارية للقهوة من مباشر إلى المستهلك معرفة ما إذا كان كوبون خصم $5 يسبب بالفعل طلبات متكررة، أم أن الأشخاص الذين يستخدمونه كانوا سيعيدون الطلب على أي حال.

segments.src: Which research design fits?
segments.tr: ما تصميم البحث المناسب؟

segments.src: - A. Exploratory — run two focus groups about coupons
segments.tr: - أ. استكشافي — أجرِ مجموعتي تركيز عن القسائم

segments.src: - B. Descriptive — survey customers on how much they like coupons
segments.tr: - ب. وصفي — استطلع العملاء عن مدى إعجابهم بالقسائم

segments.src: - C. Causal — randomly give the coupon to one group, withhold it from a comparable group, compare reorder rates
segments.tr: - ج. سببي — أعطِ القسيمة عشوائياً لمجموعة واحدة، احجب عن مجموعة مماثلة، قارن معدلات إعادة الطلب

segments.src: - D. Secondary — buy an industry report on coupon usage
segments.tr: - د. ثانوي — اشترِ تقرير صناعي عن استخدام القسائم

segments.src: **2.** True or False: "Is our checkout fast and easy?"
segments.tr: **2.** صح أم خطأ: "هل استخراج الخروج لدينا سريع وسهل؟"

segments.src: is a well-written survey question.
segments.tr: هو سؤال استطلاع مكتوب بشكل جيد.

segments.src: **3.** A shopper who has already paid $1,400 keeps rereading reviews to reassure herself she chose right.
segments.tr: **3.** متسوق دفع بالفعل $1,400 يستمر في إعادة قراءة المراجعات لتطمين نفسها بأنها اختارت بشكل صحيح.

segments.src: Which stage is this?
segments.tr: ما هذه المرحلة؟

segments.src: - A. Problem recognition
segments.tr: - أ. الاعتراف بالمشكلة

segments.src: - B. Information search
segments.tr: - ب. البحث عن المعلومات

segments.src: - C. Purchase decision
segments.tr: - ج. قرار الشراء

segments.src: - D. Post-purchase behavior
segments.tr: - د. السلوك بعد الشراء

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Secondary data** — information collected by someone else for another purpose (Census tables, trade reports, your own past sales); cheap and fast, but rarely a perfect fit for your question.
segments.tr: - **البيانات الثانوية** — معلومات جمعها شخص آخر لغرض آخر (جداول الإحصاء السكاني، تقارير التجارة، مبيعاتك الماضية)؛ رخيصة وسريعة، لكن نادراً ما تكون مناسبة تماماً لسؤالك.

segments.src: - **Probability sample** — a sample in which every member of the sampling frame has a known, non-zero chance of being selected; the precondition that makes margin of error meaningful.
segments.tr: - **عينة احتمالية** — عينة يمتلك فيها كل عضو من إطار العينة فرصة معروفة وغير صفرية للاختيار؛ الشرط المسبق الذي يجعل هامش الخطأ ذا معنى.

segments.src: - **Non-response bias** — distortion that occurs when the people who don't answer differ systematically from those who do; more responses don't fix it.
segments.tr: - **تحيز عدم الاستجابة** — تشويه يحدث عندما يختلف الأشخاص الذين لا يجيبون بشكل منهجي عن أولئك الذين يجيبون؛ المزيد من الاستجابات لا تصلحها.

segments.src: - **Consideration set** — the small handful of brands a buyer actually weighs at the evaluation stage; being known but not in the set is a distinct problem from being unknown.
segments.tr: - **مجموعة الاعتبار** — حفنة صغيرة من العلامات التجارية التي يزنها المشتري فعلاً في مرحلة التقييم؛ كونك معروفاً لكن ليس في المجموعة هو مشكلة مختلفة عن كونك غير معروف.

segments.src: - **Post-purchase dissonance** — the doubt a buyer feels after committing, especially on high-involvement purchases; managing it drives returns, reviews, and repeat business.
segments.tr: - **الفجوة بعد الشراء** — الشك الذي يشعر به المشتري بعد الالتزام، خاصة في المشتريات عالية الانخراط؛ إدارتها تقود الإرجاعات والمراجعات والأعمال المتكررة.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Only a controlled experiment separates "the coupon caused the reorder" from "reorder-prone customers redeem coupons."
segments.tr: *الإجابات: **1 — ج.** فقط التجربة المراقبة تفصل "القسيمة سببت إعادة الطلب" عن "العملاء المعرضون لإعادة الطلب يستخدمون القسائم."

segments.src: A survey measures opinion about coupons, not their effect.
segments.tr: يقيس الاستطلاع الرأي حول القسائم، وليس تأثيرها.

segments.src: **2 — False.** It's double-barreled ("fast" and "easy" are two questions with possibly opposite answers) and leading.
segments.tr: **2 — خطأ.** إنه مزدوج البرميل ("سريع" و"سهل" هما سؤالان قد يكون لهما إجابات معاكسة) وموجه.

segments.src: Split it into two neutral items.
segments.tr: قسمه إلى عنصرين محايدين.

segments.src: **3 — D.** Rereading reviews after paying is post-purchase dissonance, not information search — the search is over; she's now reducing doubt about a decision already made.*
segments.tr: **3 — د.** إعادة قراءة المراجعات بعد الدفع هي فجوة بعد الشراء، وليس البحث عن المعلومات — انتهى البحث؛ الآن تقلل من الشك حول قرار تم اتخاذه بالفعل.*

fr.title: [Marketing 101 #3] Les gens ne mentent pas dans les sondages — Ils ne savent tout simplement pas pourquoi ils achètent

segments.src: > Good market research isn't about asking customers what they want; it's about designing a question honest enough that the answer means something — then reading it against how people actually decide.
segments.tr: > La bonne recherche marketing ne consiste pas à demander aux clients ce qu'ils veulent ; il s'agit de concevoir une question suffisamment honnête pour que la réponse ait du sens — puis de la confronter à la manière dont les gens décident réellement.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: This lesson has two halves that only work when you put them together.
segments.tr: Cette leçon comporte deux parties qui ne fonctionnent que lorsque vous les mettez ensemble.

segments.src: **Half one: research design.** Marketing research is a process, not a survey link.
segments.tr: **Première partie : la conception de la recherche.** La recherche marketing est un processus, pas un lien de sondage.

segments.src: It runs: define the decision you need to make → choose a design → collect data → analyze → act.
segments.tr: Elle se déroule ainsi : définir la décision que vous devez prendre → choisir une conception → collecter des données → analyser → agir.

segments.src: Skipping straight to "let's send out a survey" is the single most common way companies buy expensive noise.
segments.tr: Passer directement à « envoyons un sondage » est le moyen le plus courant pour les entreprises d'acheter du bruit coûteux.

segments.src: Start with **secondary data** — information someone already collected.
segments.tr: Commencez par les **données secondaires** — les informations que quelqu'un d'autre a déjà collectées.

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: U.S.

segments.src: Census and Bureau of Labor Statistics tables, trade association reports, Google Trends, and above all your own sales and support logs.
segments.tr: Les tableaux du Census et du Bureau of Labor Statistics, les rapports des associations commerciales, Google Trends, et surtout vos propres logs de ventes et d'assistance.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast, but it was gathered for someone else's question, so it rarely answers yours exactly.
segments.tr: C'est bon marché et rapide, mais c'a été collecté pour la question de quelqu'un d'autre, donc cela répond rarement exactement à la vôtre.

segments.src: When you need **primary data** — data you collect yourself — pick the design that matches what you don't know:
segments.tr: Quand vous avez besoin de **données primaires** — des données que vous collectez vous-même — choisissez la conception qui correspond à ce que vous ne savez pas :

segments.src: - **Exploratory** — "What's even going on here?" In-depth interviews, focus groups, open-ended questions. Output is hypotheses, not numbers.
segments.tr: - **Exploratoire** — « Que se passe-t-il ici ? » Entretiens approfondis, groupes de discussion, questions ouvertes. Le résultat est des hypothèses, pas des chiffres.

segments.src: - **Descriptive** — "How many, how often, who?" Surveys, panels, observation. Output is a measurement.
segments.tr: - **Descriptive** — « Combien, à quelle fréquence, qui ? » Sondages, panels, observation. Le résultat est une mesure.

segments.src: - **Causal** — "Does X actually cause Y?" Controlled experiments and A/B tests, where you change one thing and hold the rest steady.
segments.tr: - **Causale** — « X cause-t-il réellement Y ? » Expériences contrôlées et tests A/B, où vous changez une chose et maintenez le reste constant.

segments.src: The classic blunder is running a descriptive survey before you've done any exploratory work — you end up precisely measuring the wrong thing.
segments.tr: L'erreur classique est de mener une enquête descriptive avant d'avoir fait un travail exploratoire — vous finissez par mesurer précisément la mauvaise chose.

segments.src: **Survey craft, briefly.** Two things decide whether a survey is worth reading:
segments.tr: **La conception d'un sondage, brièvement.** Deux choses décident si un sondage vaut la peine d'être lu :

segments.src: 1. *Who answered.* Your **sampling frame** is the list you drew from; a **probability sample** gives everyone in that frame a known chance of selection, which is what makes margin of error meaningful. A convenience sample — your Instagram followers, people who clicked the email — doesn't. Sample size matters less than most people think, and depends barely at all on population size: roughly `n = 1,000 → about ±3 percentage points` at 95% confidence, whether you're describing Rhode Island or the entire country. **Non-response bias** is the bigger threat: if only your happiest and angriest customers reply, more responses just make a skewed picture look confident.
segments.tr: 1. *Qui a répondu.* Votre **cadre d'échantillonnage** est la liste dont vous avez tiré l'échantillon ; un **échantillon probabiliste** donne à chacun dans ce cadre une probabilité connue d'être sélectionné, ce qui est ce qui rend la marge d'erreur significative. Un échantillon de convenance — vos abonnés Instagram, les personnes qui ont cliqué sur l'e-mail — non. La taille de l'échantillon importe moins que la plupart des gens le pensent, et dépend à peine de la taille de la population : à peu près `n = 1 000 → environ ±3 points de pourcentage` avec un intervalle de confiance de 95 %, que vous décriviez Rhode Island ou le pays entier. **Le biais de non-réponse** est la menace la plus grande : si seuls vos clients les plus heureux et les plus en colère répondent, plus de réponses font juste ressembler une image biaisée à quelque chose de fiable.

segments.src: 2. *What you asked.* Watch for **leading** questions ("How much did you enjoy our new checkout?"), **double-barreled** ones ("Is our checkout fast and easy?" — which half are you answering?), and **social desirability bias**, where people report the flattering answer. Then there's the **say-do gap**: stated purchase intent reliably overstates real purchasing, especially about price and about virtuous behavior. "Would you pay $30 a month for this?" is nearly worthless. "What are you paying today, and what did you do the last time you needed this?" is not.
segments.tr: 2. *Ce que vous avez demandé.* Attention aux questions **suggestives** (« Combien avez-vous aimé notre nouveau panier ? »), aux questions **à double tranchant** (« Notre panier est-il rapide et facile ? » — à quelle moitié répondez-vous ?), et au **biais de désirabilité sociale**, où les gens rapportent la réponse flatteuse. Puis il y a l'**écart parole-action** : l'intention d'achat déclarée surestime systématiquement l'achat réel, en particulier sur le prix et sur les comportements vertueux. « Paieriez-vous 30 $ par mois pour cela ? » est presque inutile. « Combien payez-vous aujourd'hui, et qu'avez-vous fait la dernière fois que vous aviez besoin de cela ? » ne l'est pas.

segments.src: **Half two: how buyers actually decide.** The standard model has five stages:
segments.tr: **Deuxième partie : comment les acheteurs décident réellement.** Le modèle standard comporte cinq étapes :

segments.src: 1. **Problem recognition** — a gap opens between where you are and where you want to be.
segments.tr: 1. **Reconnaissance du problème** — un écart s'ouvre entre où vous êtes et où vous voulez être.

segments.src: 2. **Information search** — internal (memory) first, then external (reviews, friends, retail floors).
segments.tr: 2. **Recherche d'informations** — interne (mémoire) d'abord, puis externe (avis, amis, magasins).

segments.src: 3. **Evaluation of alternatives** — a short **consideration set** gets scored on a handful of **evaluative criteria**.
segments.tr: 3. **Évaluation des alternatives** — un petit **ensemble de considération** est évalué selon quelques **critères d'évaluation**.

segments.src: 4. **Purchase decision** — plus the last-second friction that kills it: shipping cost, out of stock, a bad checkout.
segments.tr: 4. **Décision d'achat** — plus la friction de dernière seconde qui l'anéantit : les frais d'expédition, les ruptures de stock, un mauvais panier.

segments.src: 5. **Post-purchase behavior** — satisfaction, **post-purchase dissonance** (buyer's remorse), returns, reviews, repeat business.
segments.tr: 5. **Comportement post-achat** — satisfaction, **dissonance post-achat** (regret de l'acheteur), retours, avis, nouvelles commandes.

segments.src: Not every purchase runs the full loop.
segments.tr: Chaque achat ne suit pas la boucle complète.

segments.src: **High-involvement** buys — expensive, risky, identity-relevant — get the extended treatment.
segments.tr: Les achats à **implication élevée** — coûteux, risqués, identitaires — reçoivent le traitement étendu.

segments.src: Low-involvement ones (toothpaste, gas station coffee) are mostly habit, which is why for those categories the real battleground is availability and cue, not persuasion.
segments.tr: Les achats à faible implication (dentifrice, café de station-essence) sont surtout des habitudes, c'est pourquoi pour ces catégories le vrai champ de bataille est la disponibilité et l'indice, pas la persuasion.

segments.src: Put the halves together and you get the useful rule: **choose your research design based on the stage where you're losing people.**
segments.tr: Mettez les deux parties ensemble et vous obtenez la règle utile : **choisissez votre conception de recherche en fonction de l'étape où vous perdez des gens.**

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Maya moves into a one-bedroom in Denver and, on night three, wakes up with her lower back aching.
segments.tr: Maya emménage dans un T2 à Denver et, la troisième nuit, se réveille avec un mal de bas du dos.

segments.src: That's **problem recognition** — nothing about her mattress changed, but her tolerance did.
segments.tr: C'est la **reconnaissance du problème** — rien n'a changé à propos de son matelas, mais sa tolérance si.

segments.src: **Information search:** she texts two friends, reads a "best mattress 2026" roundup, watches a YouTube teardown, and — because she's spending real money — drives to a store on Colorado Boulevard to lie on three of them for ninety seconds each.
segments.tr: **Recherche d'informations :** elle envoie des SMS à deux amies, lit un résumé « meilleur matelas 2026 », regarde un démontage YouTube, et — parce qu'elle dépense de l'argent — se rend dans un magasin sur Colorado Boulevard pour s'allonger sur trois d'entre eux pendant quatre-vingt-dix secondes chacun.

segments.src: **Evaluation of alternatives:** her **consideration set** narrows to three brands.
segments.tr: **Évaluation des alternatives :** son **ensemble de considération** se réduit à trois marques.

segments.src: Her **evaluative criteria** turn out to be firmness, a sleep trial she can actually use, and price under about $1,500.
segments.tr: Ses **critères d'évaluation** s'avèrent être la fermeté, un essai de sommeil qu'elle peut réellement utiliser, et un prix inférieur à environ 1 500 $.

segments.src: Note that "made in the USA" was in the ad that got her attention but never made her criteria list — attention and criteria are different things.
segments.tr: Notez que « fabriqué aux USA » était dans l'annonce qui a attiré son attention mais n'a jamais figuré dans sa liste de critères — l'attention et les critères sont des choses différentes.

segments.src: **Purchase decision:** she picks a $1,400 queen at 11 p.m., then almost bails when old-mattress removal costs $99 extra.
segments.tr: **Décision d'achat :** elle choisit un queen à 1 400 $ à 23 h, puis est sur le point d'abandonner quand le retrait de l'ancien matelas coûte 99 $ de plus.

segments.src: Free removal in the cart is what closes it.
segments.tr: Le retrait gratuit dans le panier est ce qui conclut la vente.

segments.src: **Post-purchase:** week one is rough.
segments.tr: **Post-achat :** la première semaine est difficile.

segments.src: She rereads the reviews she already read, looking for someone saying "it takes two weeks to adjust."
segments.tr: Elle relit les avis qu'elle a déjà lus, cherchant quelqu'un disant « cela prend deux semaines pour s'adapter. »

segments.src: That's **post-purchase dissonance**, and it's the moment brands either earn a five-star review or a return.
segments.tr: C'est la **dissonance post-achat**, et c'est le moment où les marques gagnent soit un avis à cinq étoiles, soit un retour.

segments.src: Now flip to the mattress company's side.
segments.tr: Maintenant, retournez au côté de la compagnie de matelas.

segments.src: If Maya's story is typical, the research plan writes itself, stage by stage:
segments.tr: Si l'histoire de Maya est typique, le plan de recherche s'écrit de lui-même, étape par étape :

segments.src: - Suspect people don't know what firmness they need? That's fuzzy — run **exploratory** interviews with recent buyers.
segments.tr: - Soupçonnez que les gens ne savent pas quelle fermeté ils ont besoin ? C'est flou — menez des entretiens **exploratoires** avec des acheteurs récents.

segments.src: - Want to know what share of buyers rank a sleep trial above price? That's a count — run a **descriptive** survey on a probability sample of the customer list, and chase non-responders so it isn't just the enthusiasts.
segments.tr: - Voulez-vous savoir quelle proportion d'acheteurs classent un essai de sommeil au-dessus du prix ? C'est un dénombrement — menez une enquête **descriptive** sur un échantillon probabiliste de la liste de clients, et relancez les non-répondants pour que ce ne soit pas seulement les enthousiastes.

segments.src: - Think free removal lifts conversion? Don't survey it — people are terrible at reporting what a $99 fee does to them. Run a **causal** A/B test at checkout and watch behavior.
segments.tr: - Pensez que le retrait gratuit augmente la conversion ? Ne le sondez pas — les gens sont terribles pour rapporter ce qu'une redevance de 99 $ leur fait. Menez un test A/B **causal** au panier et observez le comportement.

segments.src: - Worried about returns in week two? That's a post-purchase problem, and the fix is probably an email on day 5 explaining the adjustment period, not a better ad.
segments.tr: - Préoccupé par les retours à la deuxième semaine ? C'est un problème post-achat, et la solution est probablement un e-mail au jour 5 expliquant la période d'adaptation, pas une meilleure annonce.

segments.src: 1. Match the design to the question: exploratory to find hypotheses, descriptive to measure them, causal to prove what drives what — and check secondary data before you spend a dollar on primary.

segments.src: 2. A survey is only as good as who answered and how you asked; non-response bias, leading or double-barreled wording, and the say-do gap ruin more studies than small sample sizes do.

segments.src: 3. Buyers move through problem recognition → search → evaluation → purchase → post-purchase, and the stage where you're losing them tells you which research to run.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Les termes d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: - **Secondary data** — information collected by someone else for another purpose (Census tables, trade reports, your own past sales); cheap and fast, but rarely a perfect fit for your question.
segments.tr: - **Données secondaires** — des informations collectées par quelqu'un d'autre à une autre fin (tableaux du Census, rapports commerciaux, vos ventes passées) ; bon marché et rapide, mais rarement un ajustement parfait pour votre question.

segments.src: - **Probability sample** — a sample in which every member of the sampling frame has a known, non-zero chance of being selected; the precondition that makes margin of error meaningful.
segments.tr: - **Échantillon probabiliste** — un échantillon dans lequel chaque membre du cadre d'échantillonnage a une probabilité connue et non nulle d'être sélectionné ; la condition préalable qui rend la marge d'erreur significative.

segments.src: - **Non-response bias** — distortion that occurs when the people who don't answer differ systematically from those who do; more responses don't fix it.
segments.tr: - **Biais de non-réponse** — la distorsion qui se produit quand les personnes qui ne répondent pas diffèrent systématiquement de celles qui répondent ; plus de réponses ne le règlent pas.

segments.src: - **Consideration set** — the small handful of brands a buyer actually weighs at the evaluation stage; being known but not in the set is a distinct problem from being unknown.
segments.tr: - **Ensemble de considération** — la petite poignée de marques qu'un acheteur considère réellement à l'étape d'évaluation ; être connu mais pas dans l'ensemble est un problème distinct d'être inconnu.

segments.src: - **Post-purchase dissonance** — the doubt a buyer feels after committing, especially on high-involvement purchases; managing it drives returns, reviews, and repeat business.
segments.tr: - **Dissonance post-achat** — le doute qu'un acheteur ressent après s'être engagé, surtout sur les achats à implication élevée ; la gérer détermine les retours, les avis et les nouvelles commandes.

pt.title: [Marketing 101 #3] As Pessoas Não Mentem em Pesquisas — Elas Simplesmente Não Sabem Por Que Compram

segments.src: > Good market research isn't about asking customers what they want; it's about designing a question honest enough that the answer means something — then reading it against how people actually decide.
segments.tr: > Uma boa pesquisa de mercado não se trata de perguntar aos clientes o que eles querem; trata-se de projetar uma pergunta honesta o suficiente para que a resposta signifique algo — e depois interpretá-la em relação a como as pessoas realmente decidem.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: This lesson has two halves that only work when you put them together.
segments.tr: Esta lição tem duas partes que só funcionam quando você as junta.

segments.src: **Half one: research design.** Marketing research is a process, not a survey link.
segments.tr: **Primeira parte: design de pesquisa.** A pesquisa de marketing é um processo, não um link de pesquisa.

segments.src: It runs: define the decision you need to make → choose a design → collect data → analyze → act.
segments.tr: Funciona assim: defina a decisão que você precisa tomar → escolha um design → colete dados → analise → aja.

segments.src: Skipping straight to "let's send out a survey" is the single most common way companies buy expensive noise.
segments.tr: Pular direto para "vamos enviar uma pesquisa" é a forma mais comum pela qual as empresas compram ruído caro.

segments.src: Start with **secondary data** — information someone already collected.
segments.tr: Comece com **dados secundários** — informações que alguém já coletou.

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: U.S.

segments.src: Census and Bureau of Labor Statistics tables, trade association reports, Google Trends, and above all your own sales and support logs.
segments.tr: tabelas do Census e do Bureau of Labor Statistics, relatórios de associações comerciais, Google Trends e, acima de tudo, seus próprios registros de vendas e suporte.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast, but it was gathered for someone else's question, so it rarely answers yours exactly.
segments.tr: É barato e rápido, mas foi coletado para a pergunta de outra pessoa, então raramente responde a sua exatamente.

segments.src: When you need **primary data** — data you collect yourself — pick the design that matches what you don't know:
segments.tr: Quando você precisa de **dados primários** — dados que você coleta você mesmo — escolha o design que corresponde ao que você não sabe:

segments.src: - **Exploratory** — "What's even going on here?" In-depth interviews, focus groups, open-ended questions. Output is hypotheses, not numbers.
segments.tr: - **Exploratória** — "O que está acontecendo aqui?" Entrevistas aprofundadas, grupos de foco, perguntas abertas. O resultado são hipóteses, não números.

segments.src: - **Descriptive** — "How many, how often, who?" Surveys, panels, observation. Output is a measurement.
segments.tr: - **Descritiva** — "Quantos, com que frequência, quem?" Pesquisas, painéis, observação. O resultado é uma medição.

segments.src: - **Causal** — "Does X actually cause Y?" Controlled experiments and A/B tests, where you change one thing and hold the rest steady.
segments.tr: - **Causal** — "X realmente causa Y?" Experimentos controlados e testes A/B, onde você muda uma coisa e mantém o resto constante.

segments.src: The classic blunder is running a descriptive survey before you've done any exploratory work — you end up precisely measuring the wrong thing.
segments.tr: O erro clássico é executar uma pesquisa descritiva antes de ter feito qualquer trabalho exploratório — você acaba medindo precisamente a coisa errada.

segments.src: **Survey craft, briefly.** Two things decide whether a survey is worth reading:
segments.tr: **Técnica de pesquisa, resumidamente.** Duas coisas decidem se uma pesquisa vale a pena ler:

segments.src: 1. *Who answered.* Your **sampling frame** is the list you drew from; a **probability sample** gives everyone in that frame a known chance of selection, which is what makes margin of error meaningful. A convenience sample — your Instagram followers, people who clicked the email — doesn't. Sample size matters less than most people think, and depends barely at all on population size: roughly `n = 1,000 → about ±3 percentage points` at 95% confidence, whether you're describing Rhode Island or the entire country. **Non-response bias** is the bigger threat: if only your happiest and angriest customers reply, more responses just make a skewed picture look confident.
segments.tr: 1. *Quem respondeu.* Seu **marco amostral** é a lista de onde você sacou; uma **amostra probabilística** dá a todos nesse marco uma chance conhecida de seleção, o que é o que torna a margem de erro significativa. Uma amostra de conveniência — seus seguidores do Instagram, pessoas que clicaram no email — não. O tamanho da amostra importa menos do que a maioria das pessoas pensa, e depende quase nada do tamanho da população: aproximadamente `n = 1,000 → about ±3 percentage points` com 95% de confiança, quer você esteja descrevendo Rhode Island ou todo o país. **Viés de não-resposta** é a ameaça maior: se apenas seus clientes mais felizes e mais furiosos responderem, mais respostas apenas tornam uma imagem distorcida parecer confiante.

segments.src: 2. *What you asked.* Watch for **leading** questions ("How much did you enjoy our new checkout?"), **double-barreled** ones ("Is our checkout fast and easy?" — which half are you answering?), and **social desirability bias**, where people report the flattering answer. Then there's the **say-do gap**: stated purchase intent reliably overstates real purchasing, especially about price and about virtuous behavior. "Would you pay $30 a month for this?" is nearly worthless. "What are you paying today, and what did you do the last time you needed this?" is not.
segments.tr: 2. *O que você perguntou.* Cuidado com perguntas **tendenciosas** ("Quanto você gostou de nosso novo checkout?"), perguntas **duplas** ("Nosso checkout é rápido e fácil?" — qual metade você está respondendo?), e **viés de desejabilidade social**, onde as pessoas relatam a resposta lisonjeira. Depois há a **lacuna entre o dito e o feito**: a intenção de compra declarada consistentemente exagera as compras reais, especialmente sobre preço e sobre comportamento virtuoso. "Você pagaria $30 por mês por isso?" é quase inútil. "Quanto você está pagando hoje e o que você fez na última vez que precisava disso?" não é.

segments.src: **Half two: how buyers actually decide.** The standard model has five stages:
segments.tr: **Segunda parte: como os compradores realmente decidem.** O modelo padrão tem cinco estágios:

segments.src: 1. **Problem recognition** — a gap opens between where you are and where you want to be.
segments.tr: 1. **Reconhecimento de problema** — uma lacuna se abre entre onde você está e onde quer estar.

segments.src: 2. **Information search** — internal (memory) first, then external (reviews, friends, retail floors).
segments.tr: 2. **Busca de informações** — interna (memória) primeiro, depois externa (avaliações, amigos, pisos de varejo).

segments.src: 3. **Evaluation of alternatives** — a short **consideration set** gets scored on a handful of **evaluative criteria**.
segments.tr: 3. **Avaliação de alternativas** — um curto **conjunto de consideração** é pontuado em um punhado de **critérios avaliativos**.

segments.src: 4. **Purchase decision** — plus the last-second friction that kills it: shipping cost, out of stock, a bad checkout.
segments.tr: 4. **Decisão de compra** — mais o atrito de último segundo que a destrói: custo de envio, fora de estoque, um checkout ruim.

segments.src: 5. **Post-purchase behavior** — satisfaction, **post-purchase dissonance** (buyer's remorse), returns, reviews, repeat business.
segments.tr: 5. **Comportamento pós-compra** — satisfação, **dissonância pós-compra** (arrependimento do comprador), devoluções, avaliações, negócios repetidos.

segments.src: Not every purchase runs the full loop.
segments.tr: Nem toda compra passa pelo loop completo.

segments.src: **High-involvement** buys — expensive, risky, identity-relevant — get the extended treatment.
segments.tr: Compras **de alto envolvimento** — caras, arriscadas, relevantes para a identidade — recebem o tratamento estendido.

segments.src: Low-involvement ones (toothpaste, gas station coffee) are mostly habit, which is why for those categories the real battleground is availability and cue, not persuasion.
segments.tr: As de baixo envolvimento (pasta de dente, café de posto de gasolina) são principalmente hábito, e é por isso que para essas categorias o verdadeiro campo de batalha é disponibilidade e deixa, não persuasão.

segments.src: Put the halves together and you get the useful rule: **choose your research design based on the stage where you're losing people.**
segments.tr: Junte as duas partes e você obtém a regra útil: **escolha seu design de pesquisa com base no estágio onde você está perdendo pessoas.**

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Maya moves into a one-bedroom in Denver and, on night three, wakes up with her lower back aching.
segments.tr: Maya se muda para um apartamento de um quarto em Denver e, na terceira noite, acorda com as costas doendo.

segments.src: That's **problem recognition** — nothing about her mattress changed, but her tolerance did.
segments.tr: Isso é **reconhecimento de problema** — nada sobre seu colchão mudou, mas sua tolerância mudou.

segments.src: **Information search:** she texts two friends, reads a "best mattress 2026" roundup, watches a YouTube teardown, and — because she's spending real money — drives to a store on Colorado Boulevard to lie on three of them for ninety seconds each.
segments.tr: **Busca de informações:** ela envia mensagens para dois amigos, lê um resumo de "melhor colchão 2026", assiste a uma análise do YouTube e — porque está gastando dinheiro de verdade — dirige para uma loja na Colorado Boulevard para deitar em três deles por noventa segundos cada.

segments.src: **Evaluation of alternatives:** her **consideration set** narrows to three brands.
segments.tr: **Avaliação de alternativas:** seu **conjunto de consideração** se reduz a três marcas.

segments.src: Her **evaluative criteria** turn out to be firmness, a sleep trial she can actually use, and price under about $1,500.
segments.tr: Seus **critérios avaliativos** acabam sendo firmeza, um teste de sono que ela pode realmente usar, e preço abaixo de cerca de $1,500.

segments.src: Note that "made in the USA" was in the ad that got her attention but never made her criteria list — attention and criteria are different things.
segments.tr: Observe que "fabricado nos EUA" estava no anúncio que chamou sua atenção, mas nunca entrou em sua lista de critérios — atenção e critérios são coisas diferentes.

segments.src: **Purchase decision:** she picks a $1,400 queen at 11 p.m., then almost bails when old-mattress removal costs $99 extra.
segments.tr: **Decisão de compra:** ela escolhe um queen de $1,400 às 11 p.m., depois quase desiste quando a remoção do colchão velho custa $99 a mais.

segments.src: Free removal in the cart is what closes it.
segments.tr: Remoção grátis no carrinho é o que fecha.

segments.src: **Post-purchase:** week one is rough.
segments.tr: **Pós-compra:** a primeira semana é áspera.

segments.src: She rereads the reviews she already read, looking for someone saying "it takes two weeks to adjust."
segments.tr: Ela relê as avaliações que já leu, procurando por alguém dizendo "leva duas semanas para se ajustar."

segments.src: That's **post-purchase dissonance**, and it's the moment brands either earn a five-star review or a return.
segments.tr: Essa é a **dissonância pós-compra**, e é o momento em que as marcas ganham uma avaliação de cinco estrelas ou uma devolução.
