segments.src: - **Secondary data** — information collected by someone else for another purpose (Census tables, trade reports, your own past sales); cheap and fast, but rarely a perfect fit for your question.
segments.tr: - **Dados secundários** — informações coletadas por outra pessoa para outro propósito (tabelas do Census, relatórios comerciais, suas vendas passadas); barato e rápido, mas raramente um ajuste perfeito para sua pergunta.

segments.src: - **Probability sample** — a sample in which every member of the sampling frame has a known, non-zero chance of being selected; the precondition that makes margin of error meaningful.
segments.tr: - **Amostra probabilística** — uma amostra na qual cada membro do marco amostral tem uma chance conhecida e não-zero de ser selecionado; a pré-condição que torna a margem de erro significativa.

segments.src: - **Non-response bias** — distortion that occurs when the people who don't answer differ systematically from those who do; more responses don't fix it.
segments.tr: - **Viés de não-resposta** — distorção que ocorre quando as pessoas que não respondem diferem sistematicamente daquelas que respondem; mais respostas não corrigem isso.

segments.src: - **Consideration set** — the small handful of brands a buyer actually weighs at the evaluation stage; being known but not in the set is a distinct problem from being unknown.
segments.tr: - **Conjunto de consideração** — o pequeno punhado de marcas que um comprador realmente pesa no estágio de avaliação; ser conhecido mas não estar no conjunto é um problema distinto de ser desconhecido.

segments.src: - **Post-purchase dissonance** — the doubt a buyer feels after committing, especially on high-involvement purchases; managing it drives returns, reviews, and repeat business.
segments.tr: - **Dissonância pós-compra** — a dúvida que um comprador sente após se comprometer, especialmente em compras de alto envolvimento; gerenciá-la impulsiona devoluções, avaliações e negócios repetidos.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Only a controlled experiment separates "the coupon caused the reorder" from "reorder-prone customers redeem coupons."
segments.tr: *Respostas: **1 — C.** Apenas um experimento controlado separa "o cupom causou a reorder" de "clientes propensos a reorder resgatam cupons."

segments.src: A survey measures opinion about coupons, not their effect.
segments.tr: Uma pesquisa mede opinião sobre cupons, não seu efeito.

segments.src: **2 — False.** It's double-barreled ("fast" and "easy" are two questions with possibly opposite answers) and leading.
segments.tr: **2 — Falso.** É dupla ("rápido" e "fácil" são duas perguntas com possíveis respostas opostas) e tendenciosa.

segments.src: Split it into two neutral items.
segments.tr: Divida em dois itens neutros.

segments.src: **3 — D.** Rereading reviews after paying is post-purchase dissonance, not information search — the search is over; she's now reducing doubt about a decision already made.*
segments.tr: **3 — D.** Reler avaliações após pagar é dissonância pós-compra, não busca de informações — a busca acabou; ela agora está reduzindo a dúvida sobre uma decisão já tomada.*

in.title: [Marketing 101 #3] Orang-Orang Tidak Berbohong di Survei — Mereka Hanya Tidak Tahu Mengapa Mereka Membeli

segments.src: > Good market research isn't about asking customers what they want; it's about designing a question honest enough that the answer means something — then reading it against how people actually decide.
segments.tr: > Riset pasar yang baik bukan tentang menanyakan kepada pelanggan apa yang mereka inginkan; ini tentang merancang pertanyaan yang cukup jujur sehingga jawabannya bermakna — kemudian membacanya terhadap bagaimana orang benar-benar memutuskan.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: This lesson has two halves that only work when you put them together.
segments.tr: Pelajaran ini memiliki dua bagian yang hanya berfungsi ketika Anda menyatukannya.

segments.src: **Half one: research design.** Marketing research is a process, not a survey link.
segments.tr: **Bagian satu: desain riset.** Riset pemasaran adalah suatu proses, bukan tautan survei.

segments.src: It runs: define the decision you need to make → choose a design → collect data → analyze → act.
segments.tr: Ini berjalan: tentukan keputusan yang perlu Anda buat → pilih desain → kumpulkan data → analisis → tindakan.

segments.src: Skipping straight to "let's send out a survey" is the single most common way companies buy expensive noise.
segments.tr: Melompat langsung ke "mari kita kirim survei" adalah cara paling umum perusahaan membeli kebisingan yang mahal.

segments.src: Start with **secondary data** — information someone already collected.
segments.tr: Mulai dengan **data sekunder** — informasi yang sudah dikumpulkan seseorang.

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: A.S.

segments.src: Census and Bureau of Labor Statistics tables, trade association reports, Google Trends, and above all your own sales and support logs.
segments.tr: Tabel Sensus dan Biro Statistik Tenaga Kerja, laporan asosiasi perdagangan, Google Trends, dan yang paling penting log penjualan dan dukungan Anda sendiri.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast, but it was gathered for someone else's question, so it rarely answers yours exactly.
segments.tr: Ini murah dan cepat, tetapi dikumpulkan untuk pertanyaan orang lain, jadi jarang menjawab pertanyaan Anda dengan tepat.

segments.src: When you need **primary data** — data you collect yourself — pick the design that matches what you don't know:
segments.tr: Ketika Anda membutuhkan **data primer** — data yang Anda kumpulkan sendiri — pilih desain yang sesuai dengan apa yang tidak Anda ketahui:

segments.src: - **Exploratory** — "What's even going on here?" In-depth interviews, focus groups, open-ended questions. Output is hypotheses, not numbers.
segments.tr: - **Eksploratori** — "Apa yang sedang terjadi di sini?" Wawancara mendalam, kelompok fokus, pertanyaan terbuka. Output adalah hipotesis, bukan angka.

segments.src: - **Descriptive** — "How many, how often, who?" Surveys, panels, observation. Output is a measurement.
segments.tr: - **Deskriptif** — "Berapa banyak, seberapa sering, siapa?" Survei, panel, observasi. Output adalah pengukuran.

segments.src: - **Causal** — "Does X actually cause Y?" Controlled experiments and A/B tests, where you change one thing and hold the rest steady.
segments.tr: - **Kausal** — "Apakah X benar-benar menyebabkan Y?" Eksperimen terkontrol dan tes A/B, di mana Anda mengubah satu hal dan mempertahankan sisanya tetap.

segments.src: The classic blunder is running a descriptive survey before you've done any exploratory work — you end up precisely measuring the wrong thing.
segments.tr: Kesalahan klasik adalah menjalankan survei deskriptif sebelum Anda melakukan pekerjaan eksploratori apa pun — Anda berakhir dengan mengukur hal yang salah dengan tepat.

segments.src: **Survey craft, briefly.** Two things decide whether a survey is worth reading:
segments.tr: **Keahlian survei, singkatnya.** Dua hal menentukan apakah survei layak dibaca:

segments.src: 1. *Who answered.* Your **sampling frame** is the list you drew from; a **probability sample** gives everyone in that frame a known chance of selection, which is what makes margin of error meaningful. A convenience sample — your Instagram followers, people who clicked the email — doesn't. Sample size matters less than most people think, and depends barely at all on population size: roughly `n = 1,000 → about ±3 percentage points` at 95% confidence, whether you're describing Rhode Island or the entire country. **Non-response bias** is the bigger threat: if only your happiest and angriest customers reply, more responses just make a skewed picture look confident.
segments.tr: 1. *Siapa yang menjawab.* **Kerangka sampel** Anda adalah daftar yang Anda ambil; **sampel probabilitas** memberi setiap orang dalam kerangka itu kesempatan yang diketahui untuk dipilih, itulah yang membuat margin kesalahan bermakna. Sampel kenyamanan — pengikut Instagram Anda, orang yang mengklik email — tidak. Ukuran sampel penting kurang dari yang kebanyakan orang pikir, dan hampir tidak tergantung pada ukuran populasi: kira-kira `n = 1,000 → sekitar ±3 poin persentase` pada kepercayaan 95%, apakah Anda menggambarkan Rhode Island atau seluruh negara. **Bias non-respons** adalah ancaman yang lebih besar: jika hanya pelanggan tersenang dan termarah Anda yang menjawab, lebih banyak respons hanya membuat gambar yang miring terlihat percaya diri.

segments.src: 2. *What you asked.* Watch for **leading** questions ("How much did you enjoy our new checkout?"), **double-barreled** ones ("Is our checkout fast and easy?" — which half are you answering?), and **social desirability bias**, where people report the flattering answer. Then there's the **say-do gap**: stated purchase intent reliably overstates real purchasing, especially about price and about virtuous behavior. "Would you pay $30 a month for this?" is nearly worthless. "What are you paying today, and what did you do the last time you needed this?" is not.
segments.tr: 2. *Apa yang Anda tanyakan.* Waspadai pertanyaan **memandu** ("Berapa banyak Anda menikmati checkout baru kami?"), yang **berinduk ganda** ("Apakah checkout kami cepat dan mudah?" — setengah mana yang Anda jawab?), dan **bias keberlakuan sosial**, di mana orang melaporkan jawaban yang memuaskan. Kemudian ada **kesenjangan ucapan-tindakan**: niat pembelian yang dinyatakan secara andal menyatakan pembelian nyata berlebihan, terutama tentang harga dan perilaku berbudi. "Apakah Anda akan membayar $30 sebulan untuk ini?" hampir tidak berharga. "Apa yang Anda bayarkan hari ini, dan apa yang Anda lakukan terakhir kali Anda membutuhkan ini?" tidak.

segments.src: **Half two: how buyers actually decide.** The standard model has five stages:
segments.tr: **Bagian dua: bagaimana pembeli benar-benar memutuskan.** Model standar memiliki lima tahap:

segments.src: 1. **Problem recognition** — a gap opens between where you are and where you want to be.
segments.tr: 1. **Pengenalan masalah** — celah terbuka antara di mana Anda berada dan di mana Anda ingin berada.

segments.src: 2. **Information search** — internal (memory) first, then external (reviews, friends, retail floors).
segments.tr: 2. **Pencarian informasi** — internal (memori) terlebih dahulu, kemudian eksternal (ulasan, teman, lantai ritel).

segments.src: 3. **Evaluation of alternatives** — a short **consideration set** gets scored on a handful of **evaluative criteria**.
segments.tr: 3. **Evaluasi alternatif** — **set pertimbangan** singkat mendapat skor pada segelintir **kriteria evaluatif**.

segments.src: 4. **Purchase decision** — plus the last-second friction that kills it: shipping cost, out of stock, a bad checkout.
segments.tr: 4. **Keputusan pembelian** — plus gesekan detik terakhir yang membunuhnya: biaya pengiriman, kehabisan stok, checkout yang buruk.

segments.src: 5. **Post-purchase behavior** — satisfaction, **post-purchase dissonance** (buyer's remorse), returns, reviews, repeat business.
segments.tr: 5. **Perilaku pasca-pembelian** — kepuasan, **disonansi pasca-pembelian** (penyesalan pembeli), pengembalian, ulasan, bisnis berulang.

segments.src: Not every purchase runs the full loop.
segments.tr: Tidak setiap pembelian menjalani loop penuh.

segments.src: **High-involvement** buys — expensive, risky, identity-relevant — get the extended treatment.
segments.tr: **Pembelian keterlibatan tinggi** — mahal, berisiko, relevan identitas — mendapat perawatan yang diperpanjang.

segments.src: Low-involvement ones (toothpaste, gas station coffee) are mostly habit, which is why for those categories the real battleground is availability and cue, not persuasion.
segments.tr: Yang keterlibatan rendah (pasta gigi, kopi stasiun bensin) sebagian besar kebiasaan, itulah mengapa untuk kategori tersebut medan pertempuran nyata adalah ketersediaan dan isyarat, bukan persuasi.

segments.src: Put the halves together and you get the useful rule: **choose your research design based on the stage where you're losing people.**
segments.tr: Satukan kedua bagian tersebut dan Anda mendapatkan aturan yang berguna: **pilih desain riset Anda berdasarkan tahap di mana Anda kehilangan orang.**

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Maya moves into a one-bedroom in Denver and, on night three, wakes up with her lower back aching.
segments.tr: Maya pindah ke apartemen satu kamar di Denver dan, pada malam ketiga, bangun dengan punggung bawahnya sakit.

segments.src: That's **problem recognition** — nothing about her mattress changed, but her tolerance did.
segments.tr: Itu adalah **pengenalan masalah** — tidak ada yang berubah tentang kasurnya, tetapi toleransinya berubah.

segments.src: **Information search:** she texts two friends, reads a "best mattress 2026" roundup, watches a YouTube teardown, and — because she's spending real money — drives to a store on Colorado Boulevard to lie on three of them for ninety seconds each.
segments.tr: **Pencarian informasi:** dia mengirim pesan kepada dua teman, membaca ringkasan "kasur terbaik 2026", menonton video pembongkaran YouTube, dan — karena dia mengeluarkan uang nyata — berkendara ke toko di Colorado Boulevard untuk berbaring di tiga di antaranya selama sembilan puluh detik masing-masing.

segments.src: **Evaluation of alternatives:** her **consideration set** narrows to three brands.
segments.tr: **Evaluasi alternatif:** **set pertimbangan** nya menyempit menjadi tiga merek.

segments.src: Her **evaluative criteria** turn out to be firmness, a sleep trial she can actually use, and price under about $1,500.
segments.tr: **Kriteria evaluatif** nya ternyata adalah kekerasan, uji tidur yang benar-benar bisa dia gunakan, dan harga di bawah sekitar $1,500.

segments.src: Note that "made in the USA" was in the ad that got her attention but never made her criteria list — attention and criteria are different things.
segments.tr: Perhatikan bahwa "dibuat di USA" ada dalam iklan yang menarik perhatiannya tetapi tidak pernah masuk ke daftar kriterianya — perhatian dan kriteria adalah hal yang berbeda.

segments.src: **Purchase decision:** she picks a $1,400 queen at 11 p.m., then almost bails when old-mattress removal costs $99 extra.
segments.tr: **Keputusan pembelian:** dia memilih ratu $1,400 pada jam 11 malam, kemudian hampir membatalkan ketika penghapusan kasur lama biayanya $99 ekstra.

segments.src: Free removal in the cart is what closes it.
segments.tr: Penghapusan gratis di keranjang adalah apa yang menutupnya.

segments.src: **Post-purchase:** week one is rough.
segments.tr: **Pasca-pembelian:** minggu pertama sulit.

segments.src: She rereads the reviews she already read, looking for someone saying "it takes two weeks to adjust."
segments.tr: Dia membaca ulang ulasan yang sudah dia baca, mencari seseorang yang mengatakan "butuh dua minggu untuk menyesuaikan."

segments.src: That's **post-purchase dissonance**, and it's the moment brands either earn a five-star review or a return.
segments.tr: Itu adalah **disonansi pasca-pembelian**, dan itu adalah saat merek baik mendapatkan ulasan lima bintang atau pengembalian.

segments.src: Now flip to the mattress company's side.
segments.tr: Sekarang balik ke sisi perusahaan kasur.

segments.src: If Maya's story is typical, the research plan writes itself, stage by stage:
segments.tr: Jika cerita Maya adalah tipikal, rencana riset menulis sendiri, tahap demi tahap:

segments.src: - Suspect people don't know what firmness they need? That's fuzzy — run **exploratory** interviews with recent buyers.
segments.tr: - Mencurigai orang tidak tahu kekerasan apa yang mereka butuhkan? Itu kabur — jalankan wawancara **eksploratori** dengan pembeli baru.

segments.src: - Want to know what share of buyers rank a sleep trial above price? That's a count — run a **descriptive** survey on a probability sample of the customer list, and chase non-responders so it isn't just the enthusiasts.
segments.tr: - Ingin tahu berapa bagian pembeli menilai uji tidur di atas harga? Itu adalah hitungan — jalankan survei **deskriptif** pada sampel probabilitas dari daftar pelanggan, dan kejar non-responden sehingga tidak hanya penggemar.

segments.src: - Think free removal lifts conversion? Don't survey it — people are terrible at reporting what a $99 fee does to them. Run a **causal** A/B test at checkout and watch behavior.
segments.tr: - Pikirkan penghapusan gratis meningkatkan konversi? Jangan survei — orang sangat buruk dalam melaporkan apa yang biaya $99 lakukan kepada mereka. Jalankan tes A/B **kausal** di checkout dan tonton perilaku.

segments.src: - Worried about returns in week two? That's a post-purchase problem, and the fix is probably an email on day 5 explaining the adjustment period, not a better ad.
segments.tr: - Khawatir tentang pengembalian di minggu kedua? Itu adalah masalah pasca-pembelian, dan perbaikannya mungkin adalah email pada hari ke-5 yang menjelaskan periode penyesuaian, bukan iklan yang lebih baik.

segments.src: Same company, four questions, four different designs.
segments.tr: Perusahaan yang sama, empat pertanyaan, empat desain berbeda.

segments.src: A single "customer satisfaction survey" would have answered none of them well.
segments.tr: Survei "kepuasan pelanggan" tunggal tidak akan menjawab satupun dengan baik.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Match the design to the question: exploratory to find hypotheses, descriptive to measure them, causal to prove what drives what — and check secondary data before you spend a dollar on primary.
segments.tr: 1. Sesuaikan desain dengan pertanyaan: eksploratori untuk menemukan hipotesis, deskriptif untuk mengukur mereka, kausal untuk membuktikan apa yang mendorong apa — dan periksa data sekunder sebelum Anda menghabiskan satu dolar untuk data primer.

segments.src: 2. A survey is only as good as who answered and how you asked; non-response bias, leading or double-barreled wording, and the say-do gap ruin more studies than small sample sizes do.
segments.tr: 2. Survei hanya sebaik siapa yang menjawab dan bagaimana Anda bertanya; bias non-respons, fraseologi memandu atau berinduk ganda, dan kesenjangan ucapan-tindakan merusak lebih banyak studi daripada ukuran sampel kecil.

segments.src: 3. Buyers move through problem recognition → search → evaluation → purchase → post-purchase, and the stage where you're losing them tells you which research to run.
segments.tr: 3. Pembeli bergerak melalui pengenalan masalah → pencarian → evaluasi → pembelian → pasca-pembelian, dan tahap di mana Anda kehilangan mereka memberi tahu Anda penelitian mana yang harus dijalankan.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **1.** A direct-to-consumer coffee brand wants to know whether a $5-off coupon actually causes repeat orders, or whether the people who redeem it would have reordered anyway.
segments.tr: **1.** Merek kopi langsung-ke-konsumen ingin tahu apakah kupon diskon $5 benar-benar menyebabkan pesanan berulang, atau apakah orang yang menebusnya akan memesan ulang dengan cara apa pun.

segments.src: Which research design fits?
segments.tr: Desain riset mana yang sesuai?

segments.src: - A. Exploratory — run two focus groups about coupons
segments.tr: - A. Eksploratori — jalankan dua kelompok fokus tentang kupon

segments.src: - B. Descriptive — survey customers on how much they like coupons
segments.tr: - B. Deskriptif — survei pelanggan tentang seberapa banyak mereka menyukai kupon

segments.src: - C. Causal — randomly give the coupon to one group, withhold it from a comparable group, compare reorder rates
segments.tr: - C. Kausal — secara acak berikan kupon kepada satu kelompok, tahan dari kelompok yang sebanding, bandingkan tingkat pesanan ulang

segments.src: - D. Secondary — buy an industry report on coupon usage
segments.tr: - D. Sekunder — beli laporan industri tentang penggunaan kupon

segments.src: **2.** True or False: "Is our checkout fast and easy?"
segments.tr: **2.** Benar atau Salah: "Apakah checkout kami cepat dan mudah?"

segments.src: is a well-written survey question.
segments.tr: adalah pertanyaan survei yang ditulis dengan baik.

segments.src: **3.** A shopper who has already paid $1,400 keeps rereading reviews to reassure herself she chose right.
segments.tr: **3.** Seorang pembeli yang telah membayar $1,400 terus-menerus membaca ulang ulasan untuk meyakinkan dirinya bahwa dia memilih dengan benar.

segments.src: Which stage is this?
segments.tr: Tahap mana ini?

segments.src: - A. Problem recognition
segments.tr: - A. Pengenalan masalah

segments.src: - B. Information search
segments.tr: - B. Pencarian informasi

segments.src: - C. Purchase decision
segments.tr: - C. Keputusan pembelian

segments.src: - D. Post-purchase behavior
segments.tr: - D. Perilaku pasca-pembelian

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Secondary data** — information collected by someone else for another purpose (Census tables, trade reports, your own past sales); cheap and fast, but rarely a perfect fit for your question.
segments.tr: - **Data sekunder** — informasi yang dikumpulkan oleh orang lain untuk tujuan lain (tabel Sensus, laporan perdagangan, penjualan masa lalu Anda); murah dan cepat, tetapi jarang merupakan kecocokan sempurna untuk pertanyaan Anda.

segments.src: - **Probability sample** — a sample in which every member of the sampling frame has a known, non-zero chance of being selected; the precondition that makes margin of error meaningful.
segments.tr: - **Sampel probabilitas** — sampel di mana setiap anggota kerangka sampel memiliki peluang yang diketahui, bukan nol untuk dipilih; prasyarat yang membuat margin kesalahan bermakna.

segments.src: - **Non-response bias** — distortion that occurs when the people who don't answer differ systematically from those who do; more responses don't fix it.
segments.tr: - **Bias non-respons** — distorsi yang terjadi ketika orang yang tidak menjawab berbeda secara sistematis dari mereka yang menjawab; lebih banyak respons tidak akan memperbaikinya.

segments.src: - **Consideration set** — the small handful of brands a buyer actually weighs at the evaluation stage; being known but not in the set is a distinct problem from being unknown.
segments.tr: - **Set pertimbangan** — segelintir merek yang benar-benar ditimbang pembeli pada tahap evaluasi; dikenal tetapi tidak dalam set adalah masalah yang berbeda dari tidak dikenal.

segments.src: - **Post-purchase dissonance** — the doubt a buyer feels after committing, especially on high-involvement purchases; managing it drives returns, reviews, and repeat business.
segments.tr: - **Disonansi pasca-pembelian** — keraguan yang dirasakan pembeli setelah berkomitmen, terutama pada pembelian keterlibatan tinggi; mengelolaanya mendorong pengembalian, ulasan, dan bisnis berulang.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Only a controlled experiment separates "the coupon caused the reorder" from "reorder-prone customers redeem coupons."
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **1 — C.** Hanya eksperimen terkontrol yang memisahkan "kupon menyebabkan pesanan ulang" dari "pelanggan yang rentan terhadap pesanan ulang menebus kupon."

segments.src: A survey measures opinion about coupons, not their effect.
segments.tr: Survei mengukur pendapat tentang kupon, bukan efeknya.

segments.src: **2 — False.** It's double-barreled ("fast" and "easy" are two questions with possibly opposite answers) and leading.
segments.tr: **2 — Salah.** Ini berinduk ganda ("cepat" dan "mudah" adalah dua pertanyaan dengan kemungkinan jawaban yang berlawanan) dan memandu.

segments.src: Split it into two neutral items.
segments.tr: Pisahkan menjadi dua item netral.

segments.src: **3 — D.** Rereading reviews after paying is post-purchase dissonance, not information search — the search is over; she's now reducing doubt about a decision already made.*
segments.tr: **3 — D.** Membaca ulang ulasan setelah membayar adalah disonansi pasca-pembelian, bukan pencarian informasi — pencarian sudah selesai; dia sekarang mengurangi keraguan tentang keputusan yang sudah dibuat.*

segments.src: > Good market research isn't about asking customers what they want; it's about designing a question honest enough that the answer means something — then reading it against how people actually decide.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: This lesson has two halves that only work when you put them together.
segments.tr: このレッスンは、2つの部分を組み合わせてこそ機能します。

segments.src: **Half one: research design.** Marketing research is a process, not a survey link.
segments.tr: **最初の半分：リサーチデザイン。** マーケティングリサーチはプロセスであり、調査リンクではありません。

segments.src: It runs: define the decision you need to make → choose a design → collect data → analyze → act.
segments.tr: 流れは次のとおりです：必要な決定を定義する → デザインを選択する → データを収集する → 分析する → 実行する。

segments.src: Skipping straight to "let's send out a survey" is the single most common way companies buy expensive noise.
segments.tr: いきなり「調査を送ろう」とスキップすることは、企業が高額なノイズを買う最も一般的な方法です。

segments.src: Start with **secondary data** — information someone already collected.
segments.tr: **二次データ** — すでに誰かが収集した情報から始めます。

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: U.S.

segments.src: Census and Bureau of Labor Statistics tables, trade association reports, Google Trends, and above all your own sales and support logs.
segments.tr: 国勢調査と労働統計局のテーブル、業界団体のレポート、Google Trends、そして何より重要なのはあなた自身の売上とサポートログです。

segments.src: It's cheap and fast, but it was gathered for someone else's question, so it rarely answers yours exactly.
segments.tr: 安くて速いのですが、他の誰かの質問のために収集されたので、あなたの質問に正確に答えることはめったにありません。

segments.src: When you need **primary data** — data you collect yourself — pick the design that matches what you don't know:
segments.tr: **一次データ** — あなた自身が収集するデータが必要な場合 — あなたが知らないことに合致するデザインを選択します：

segments.src: - **Exploratory** — "What's even going on here?" In-depth interviews, focus groups, open-ended questions. Output is hypotheses, not numbers.
segments.tr: - **探索的** — 「ここで何が起こっているのか？」深掘りインタビュー、フォーカスグループ、オープンエンデッドな質問。アウトプットは仮説であり、数字ではありません。

segments.src: - **Descriptive** — "How many, how often, who?" Surveys, panels, observation. Output is a measurement.
segments.tr: - **記述的** — 「いくつ、どのくらいの頻度で、誰が？」調査、パネル、観察。アウトプットは測定です。

segments.src: - **Causal** — "Does X actually cause Y?" Controlled experiments and A/B tests, where you change one thing and hold the rest steady.
segments.tr: - **因果** — 「Xは実際にYを引き起こしますか？」制御実験とA/Bテスト、1つのことを変更して他はそのままにします。

segments.src: The classic blunder is running a descriptive survey before you've done any exploratory work — you end up precisely measuring the wrong thing.
segments.tr: 典型的な誤りは、探索的な作業を行う前に記述的調査を実行することです — 間違ったものを正確に測定してしまいます。

segments.src: **Survey craft, briefly.** Two things decide whether a survey is worth reading:
segments.tr: **調査作成、簡潔に。** 調査が読む価値があるかどうかを決定する2つのことがあります：

segments.src: 1. *Who answered.* Your **sampling frame** is the list you drew from; a **probability sample** gives everyone in that frame a known chance of selection, which is what makes margin of error meaningful. A convenience sample — your Instagram followers, people who clicked the email — doesn't. Sample size matters less than most people think, and depends barely at all on population size: roughly `n = 1,000 → about ±3 percentage points` at 95% confidence, whether you're describing Rhode Island or the entire country. **Non-response bias** is the bigger threat: if only your happiest and angriest customers reply, more responses just make a skewed picture look confident.
segments.tr: 1. *誰が回答したか。* あなたの **サンプリングフレーム** は抽出した対象者のリストです。**確率サンプル** はそのフレーム内のすべての人に既知の選択機会を与え、これが誤差範囲を有意にします。利便的サンプル — あなたのInstagramフォロワー、メールをクリックした人 — そうではありません。サンプルサイズは、ほとんどの人が考えるより重要ではなく、母集団サイズにほとんど依存しません：95%信頼度でおよそ `n = 1,000 → 約±3パーセントポイント`、ロードアイランド州を説明しているか国全体を説明しているかは関係ありません。**無回答バイアス** はより大きな脅威です：あなたの最も満足した顧客と最も怒った顧客だけが返信した場合、より多くの返信は、歪んだ図を自信があるように見せます。

segments.src: 2. *What you asked.* Watch for **leading** questions ("How much did you enjoy our new checkout?"), **double-barreled** ones ("Is our checkout fast and easy?" — which half are you answering?), and **social desirability bias**, where people report the flattering answer. Then there's the **say-do gap**: stated purchase intent reliably overstates real purchasing, especially about price and about virtuous behavior. "Would you pay $30 a month for this?" is nearly worthless. "What are you paying today, and what did you do the last time you needed this?" is not.
segments.tr: 2. *何を尋ねたか。* **誘導的な** 質問（「新しいチェックアウトをどの程度楽しみましたか？」）、**二重質問**（「チェックアウトは速くて簡単ですか？」— どちらの半分に答えていますか？）、**社会的望ましさバイアス**（人々が好ましい答えを報告する）に注意してください。それから **言行ギャップ** があります：述べられた購買意思は、実際の購買を確実に過大評価します、特に価格と道徳的行動について。「これに月額$30を払いますか？」はほぼ無価値です。「今日いくら払っていますか、そしてこれが必要だった最後の時に何をしましたか？」はそうではありません。

segments.src: **Half two: how buyers actually decide.** The standard model has five stages:
segments.tr: **最初の半分：買い手が実際にどのように決定するか。** 標準モデルには5つのステージがあります：

segments.src: 1. **Problem recognition** — a gap opens between where you are and where you want to be.
segments.tr: 1. **問題認識** — 現在地と望む場所の間に隔たりが開きます。

segments.src: 2. **Information search** — internal (memory) first, then external (reviews, friends, retail floors).
segments.tr: 2. **情報探索** — 内部（記憶）が最初、その後外部（レビュー、友人、小売店舗）。

segments.src: 3. **Evaluation of alternatives** — a short **consideration set** gets scored on a handful of **evaluative criteria**.
segments.tr: 3. **代替案の評価** — 短い **検討対象集合** が少数の **評価基準** でスコア化されます。

segments.src: 4. **Purchase decision** — plus the last-second friction that kills it: shipping cost, out of stock, a bad checkout.
segments.tr: 4. **購買決定** — それを殺す最後の摩擦を加えて：送料、在庫なし、不良なチェックアウト。

segments.src: 5. **Post-purchase behavior** — satisfaction, **post-purchase dissonance** (buyer's remorse), returns, reviews, repeat business.
segments.tr: 5. **購買後の行動** — 満足度、**購買後の不協和感**（買った後の悔い）、返品、レビュー、リピートビジネス。

segments.src: Not every purchase runs the full loop.
segments.tr: すべての購買がフルループを実行するわけではありません。

segments.src: **High-involvement** buys — expensive, risky, identity-relevant — get the extended treatment.
segments.tr: **高関与** の購買 — 高価で、リスキーで、自己認識に関連 — 拡張された扱いを受けます。

segments.src: Low-involvement ones (toothpaste, gas station coffee) are mostly habit, which is why for those categories the real battleground is availability and cue, not persuasion.
segments.tr: 低関与のもの（歯磨き粉、ガソリンスタンドのコーヒー）はほとんど習慣であり、これらのカテゴリーでは実際の戦場は説得ではなく入手可能性と手がかりです。

segments.src: Put the halves together and you get the useful rule: **choose your research design based on the stage where you're losing people.**
segments.tr: 2つの半分を組み合わせると、便利なルールが得られます：**人を失っているステージに基づいてリサーチデザインを選択してください。**

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活で

segments.src: Maya moves into a one-bedroom in Denver and, on night three, wakes up with her lower back aching.
segments.tr: マヤはデンバーのワンベッドルームに引っ越し、3日目の夜、腰が痛くて目を覚まします。

segments.src: That's **problem recognition** — nothing about her mattress changed, but her tolerance did.
segments.tr: これは **問題認識** です — マットレスについて何も変わりませんでしたが、彼女の耐性が変わりました。

segments.src: **Information search:** she texts two friends, reads a "best mattress 2026" roundup, watches a YouTube teardown, and — because she's spending real money — drives to a store on Colorado Boulevard to lie on three of them for ninety seconds each.
segments.tr: **情報探索：** 彼女は2人の友人にテキストを送り、「2026年最高のマットレス」のまとめを読み、YouTubeの分解を見て、そして — 彼女が本当のお金を使っているので — コロラドブルバードのストアに運転して、それぞれ90秒間、3つのマットレスに横たわります。

segments.src: **Evaluation of alternatives:** her **consideration set** narrows to three brands.
segments.tr: **代替案の評価：** 彼女の **検討対象集合** は3つのブランドに絞られます。

segments.src: Her **evaluative criteria** turn out to be firmness, a sleep trial she can actually use, and price under about $1,500.
segments.tr: 彼女の **評価基準** は、硬さ、実際に使える睡眠トライアル、および約$1,500以下の価格であることが判明します。

segments.src: Note that "made in the USA" was in the ad that got her attention but never made her criteria list — attention and criteria are different things.
segments.tr: 「made in the USA」は彼女の注意を引いた広告に含まれていましたが、彼女の基準リストに含まれることはありませんでした — 注意と基準は異なるものです。

segments.src: **Purchase decision:** she picks a $1,400 queen at 11 p.m., then almost bails when old-mattress removal costs $99 extra.
segments.tr: **購買決定：** 彼女は午後11時にクイーンサイズの$1,400を選び、古いマットレスの撤去に追加で$99かかるときにほぼ撤退します。

segments.src: Free removal in the cart is what closes it.
segments.tr: カート内の無料撤去がそれを閉じます。

segments.src: **Post-purchase:** week one is rough.
segments.tr: **購買後：** 1週目は大変です。

segments.src: She rereads the reviews she already read, looking for someone saying "it takes two weeks to adjust."
segments.tr: 彼女は既に読んだレビューを再び読み、「調整に2週間かかります」と言っている誰かを探しています。

segments.src: That's **post-purchase dissonance**, and it's the moment brands either earn a five-star review or a return.
segments.tr: これは **購買後の不協和感** であり、ブランドが5つ星のレビューまたは返品を獲得するその時です。

segments.src: Now flip to the mattress company's side.
segments.tr: それでは、マットレス会社の側に切り替えます。

segments.src: If Maya's story is typical, the research plan writes itself, stage by stage:
segments.tr: マヤのストーリーが典型的なら、リサーチプランはそれ自体を段階的に書き出します：

segments.src: - Suspect people don't know what firmness they need? That's fuzzy — run **exploratory** interviews with recent buyers.
segments.tr: - 人々が必要な硬さが何かを知らないと思いますか？それはあいまいです — 最近の買い手を対象に **探索的** インタビューを実施します。

segments.src: - Want to know what share of buyers rank a sleep trial above price? That's a count — run a **descriptive** survey on a probability sample of the customer list, and chase non-responders so it isn't just the enthusiasts.
segments.tr: - 睡眠トライアルを価格より上にランク付けする買い手のシェアを知りたいですか？それは数です — 顧客リストの確率サンプルに対して **記述的** 調査を実施し、非回答者を追跡して、熱心な人だけではないようにします。

segments.src: - Think free removal lifts conversion? Don't survey it — people are terrible at reporting what a $99 fee does to them. Run a **causal** A/B test at checkout and watch behavior.
segments.tr: - 無料撤去がコンバージョンを向上させると思いますか？調査しないでください — 人々は$99の手数料が彼らに何をするかを報告するのが下手です。チェックアウトで **因果** A/Bテストを実施して、行動を観察します。

segments.src: - Worried about returns in week two? That's a post-purchase problem, and the fix is probably an email on day 5 explaining the adjustment period, not a better ad.
segments.tr: - 2週目の返品を心配していますか？それは購買後の問題であり、修正はおそらくより良い広告ではなく、調整期間を説明する5日目のメールです。

segments.src: Same company, four questions, four different designs.
segments.tr: 同じ会社、4つの質問、4つの異なるデザイン。

segments.src: A single "customer satisfaction survey" would have answered none of them well.
segments.tr: 単一の「顧客満足度調査」では、それらのどれにもうまく答えられません。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行の要約

segments.src: 1. Match the design to the question: exploratory to find hypotheses, descriptive to measure them, causal to prove what drives what — and check secondary data before you spend a dollar on primary.
segments.tr: 1. デザインを質問に合わせます：仮説を見つけるために探索的、それらを測定するために記述的、何が何を駆動するかを証明するために因果的 — そして主要なデータに1ドルを費やす前に二次データを確認します。

segments.src: 2. A survey is only as good as who answered and how you asked; non-response bias, leading or double-barreled wording, and the say-do gap ruin more studies than small sample sizes do.
segments.tr: 2. 調査は、誰が答えたか、そしてどのように尋ねたかと同じくらい良いです。無回答バイアス、誘導的または二重質問の文言、および言行ギャップは、小さいサンプルサイズより多くの研究を台無しにします。

segments.src: 3. Buyers move through problem recognition → search → evaluation → purchase → post-purchase, and the stage where you're losing them tells you which research to run.
segments.tr: 3. 買い手は問題認識 → 検索 → 評価 → 購買 → 購買後を移動し、あなたが人を失っているステージは、実行するリサーチを示します。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自己クイズ

segments.src: **1.** A direct-to-consumer coffee brand wants to know whether a $5-off coupon actually causes repeat orders, or whether the people who redeem it would have reordered anyway.
segments.tr: **1.** ダイレクト・ツー・コンシューマーのコーヒーブランドは、$5割引クーポンが実際にリピートオーダーを引き起こすかどうか、またはそれを引き換える人々がいずれにせよ再注文したかどうかを知りたいです。

segments.src: Which research design fits?
segments.tr: どのリサーチデザインが適合していますか？

segments.src: - A. Exploratory — run two focus groups about coupons
segments.tr: - A. 探索的 — クーポンについて2つのフォーカスグループを実施します

segments.src: - B. Descriptive — survey customers on how much they like coupons
segments.tr: - B. 記述的 — クーポンをどの程度好むかについて顧客を調査します

segments.src: - C. Causal — randomly give the coupon to one group, withhold it from a comparable group, compare reorder rates
segments.tr: - C. 因果 — ランダムにクーポンを1つのグループに与え、比較可能なグループから差し控え、リオーダー率を比較します

segments.src: - D. Secondary — buy an industry report on coupon usage
segments.tr: - D. 二次 — クーポン使用に関する業界レポートを購入します

segments.src: **2.** True or False: "Is our checkout fast and easy?"
segments.tr: **2.** 真実か嘘か：「チェックアウトは速くて簡単ですか？"

segments.src: is a well-written survey question.
segments.tr: は、よく書かれた調査質問です。

segments.src: **3.** A shopper who has already paid $1,400 keeps rereading reviews to reassure herself she chose right.
segments.tr: **3.** 既に$1,400を支払った買い物客は、自分が正しい選択をしたことを自分自身に安心させるために、レビューを再読み続けています。

segments.src: Which stage is this?
segments.tr: これはどのステージですか？

segments.src: - A. Problem recognition
segments.tr: - A. 問題認識

segments.src: - B. Information search
segments.tr: - B. 情報探索

segments.src: - C. Purchase decision
segments.tr: - C. 購買決定

segments.src: - D. Post-purchase behavior
segments.tr: - D. 購買後の行動

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 本日の用語

segments.src: - **Secondary data** — information collected by someone else for another purpose (Census tables, trade reports, your own past sales); cheap and fast, but rarely a perfect fit for your question.
segments.tr: - **二次データ** — 別の目的のために他の誰かによって収集された情報（国勢調査テーブル、トレードレポート、過去の売上）；安くて速いのですが、あなたの質問に完全に適合することはめったにありません。

segments.src: - **Probability sample** — a sample in which every member of the sampling frame has a known, non-zero chance of being selected; the precondition that makes margin of error meaningful.
segments.tr: - **確率サンプル** — サンプリングフレームのすべてのメンバーが既知の非ゼロの選択機会を持つサンプル；誤差範囲を有意にする前提条件。

segments.src: - **Non-response bias** — distortion that occurs when the people who don't answer differ systematically from those who do; more responses don't fix it.
segments.tr: - **無回答バイアス** — 回答しない人が回答する人と体系的に異なるときに発生する歪み；より多くの回答はそれを修正しません。

segments.src: - **Consideration set** — the small handful of brands a buyer actually weighs at the evaluation stage; being known but not in the set is a distinct problem from being unknown.
segments.tr: - **検討対象集合** — 評価段階で買い手が実際に検討する少数のブランド；既知だが集合に含まれないことは、不明からは異なる問題です。

segments.src: - **Post-purchase dissonance** — the doubt a buyer feels after committing, especially on high-involvement purchases; managing it drives returns, reviews, and repeat business.
segments.tr: - **購買後の不協和感** — コミットした後の買い手が感じる疑い、特に高関与購買について；それを管理することは返品、レビュー、リピートビジネスを駆動します。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Only a controlled experiment separates "the coupon caused the reorder" from "reorder-prone customers redeem coupons."
segments.tr: *答え：**1 — C。** 制御された実験だけが「クーポンが再注文を引き起こした」を「再注文しやすい顧客がクーポンを引き換える」から分離します。

segments.src: A survey measures opinion about coupons, not their effect.
segments.tr: 調査はクーポンに関する意見を測定し、その効果ではありません。

segments.src: **2 — False.** It's double-barreled ("fast" and "easy" are two questions with possibly opposite answers) and leading.
segments.tr: **2 — 偽。** それは二重質問です（「速い」と「簡単」は可能性のある反対の答えを持つ2つの質問）そして誘導的です。

segments.src: Split it into two neutral items.
segments.tr: それを2つの中立的なアイテムに分割します。

segments.src: **3 — D.** Rereading reviews after paying is post-purchase dissonance, not information search — the search is over; she's now reducing doubt about a decision already made.*
segments.tr: **3 — D。** 支払った後のレビューの再読は、情報探索ではなく購買後の不協和感です — 検索は終了しています。彼女は現在、既に下された決定についての疑いを軽減しています。*

de.title: [Marketing 101 #3] Menschen lügen in Umfragen nicht — sie wissen einfach nicht, warum sie kaufen

segments.src: > Good market research isn't about asking customers what they want; it's about designing a question honest enough that the answer means something — then reading it against how people actually decide.
segments.tr: > Eine gute Marktforschung besteht nicht darin, Kunden zu fragen, was sie wollen; es geht darum, eine Frage so ehrlich zu formulieren, dass die Antwort etwas bedeutet — und dann zu lesen, wie Menschen tatsächlich entscheiden.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konzept für heute

segments.src: This lesson has two halves that only work when you put them together.
segments.tr: Diese Lektion hat zwei Teile, die nur funktionieren, wenn man sie zusammen betrachtet.

segments.src: **Half one: research design.** Marketing research is a process, not a survey link.
segments.tr: **Teil eins: Forschungsdesign.** Marktforschung ist ein Prozess, kein Umfrage-Link.

segments.src: It runs: define the decision you need to make → choose a design → collect data → analyze → act.
segments.tr: Der Ablauf: Entscheidung definieren → Design wählen → Daten sammeln → Analysieren → Handeln.

segments.src: Skipping straight to "let's send out a survey" is the single most common way companies buy expensive noise.
segments.tr: Direkt zu "lassen Sie uns eine Umfrage versenden" zu springen ist der häufigste Weg, wie Unternehmen Geld für nutzlose Daten ausgeben.

segments.src: Start with **secondary data** — information someone already collected.
segments.tr: Beginnen Sie mit **Sekundärdaten** — Informationen, die jemand bereits gesammelt hat.

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: U.S.

segments.src: Census and Bureau of Labor Statistics tables, trade association reports, Google Trends, and above all your own sales and support logs.
segments.tr: Census- und Bureau of Labor Statistics-Tabellen, Branchenverbandberichte, Google Trends und vor allem Ihre eigenen Verkaufs- und Support-Protokolle.

segments.src: It's cheap and fast, but it was gathered for someone else's question, so it rarely answers yours exactly.
segments.tr: Es ist billig und schnell, aber es wurde für jemand anderen Frage gesammelt, also beantwortet es selten Ihre Frage genau.

segments.src: When you need **primary data** — data you collect yourself — pick the design that matches what you don't know:
segments.tr: Wenn Sie **Primärdaten** benötigen — Daten, die Sie selbst sammeln — wählen Sie das Design, das zu dem passt, was Sie nicht wissen:

segments.src: - **Exploratory** — "What's even going on here?" In-depth interviews, focus groups, open-ended questions. Output is hypotheses, not numbers.
segments.tr: - **Explorative** — "Was ist hier überhaupt los?" Tiefeninterviews, Fokusgruppen, offene Fragen. Ergebnis sind Hypothesen, keine Zahlen.

segments.src: - **Descriptive** — "How many, how often, who?" Surveys, panels, observation. Output is a measurement.
segments.tr: - **Deskriptiv** — "Wie viele, wie oft, wer?" Umfragen, Panels, Beobachtung. Ergebnis ist eine Messung.

segments.src: - **Causal** — "Does X actually cause Y?" Controlled experiments and A/B tests, where you change one thing and hold the rest steady.
segments.tr: - **Kausal** — "Verursacht X wirklich Y?" Kontrollierte Experimente und A/B-Tests, bei denen Sie eine Sache ändern und den Rest konstant halten.

segments.src: The classic blunder is running a descriptive survey before you've done any exploratory work — you end up precisely measuring the wrong thing.
segments.tr: Der klassische Fehler ist, eine deskriptive Umfrage auszuführen, bevor Sie exploratorische Arbeit geleistet haben — Sie enden damit, die falsche Sache genau zu messen.

segments.src: **Survey craft, briefly.** Two things decide whether a survey is worth reading:
segments.tr: **Umfrage-Handwerk, kurz gefasst.** Zwei Dinge entscheiden, ob eine Umfrage lesenswert ist:

segments.src: 1. *Who answered.* Your **sampling frame** is the list you drew from; a **probability sample** gives everyone in that frame a known chance of selection, which is what makes margin of error meaningful. A convenience sample — your Instagram followers, people who clicked the email — doesn't. Sample size matters less than most people think, and depends barely at all on population size: roughly `n = 1,000 → about ±3 percentage points` at 95% confidence, whether you're describing Rhode Island or the entire country. **Non-response bias** is the bigger threat: if only your happiest and angriest customers reply, more responses just make a skewed picture look confident.
segments.tr: 1. *Wer antwortet.* Ihr **Stichprobenrahmen** ist die Liste, aus der Sie gezogen haben; eine **Wahrscheinlichkeitsstichprobe** gibt jedem in diesem Rahmen eine bekannte Auswahlwahrscheinlichkeit, was die Fehlermarge aussagekräftig macht. Eine Gelegenheitsstichprobe — Ihre Instagram-Follower, Menschen, die auf die E-Mail klickten — nicht. Die Stichprobengröße ist weniger wichtig als die meisten Menschen denken und hängt kaum von der Bevölkerungsgröße ab: ungefähr `n = 1,000 → etwa ±3 Prozentpunkte` bei 95% Konfidenz, ob Sie Rhode Island oder das ganze Land beschreiben. **Nichtantwort-Verzerrung** ist die größere Bedrohung: Wenn nur Ihre glücklichsten und wütendsten Kunden antworten, machen mehr Antworten nur ein verzerrtes Bild zuversichtlich aussehen.

segments.src: 2. *What you asked.* Watch for **leading** questions ("How much did you enjoy our new checkout?"), **double-barreled** ones ("Is our checkout fast and easy?" — which half are you answering?), and **social desirability bias**, where people report the flattering answer. Then there's the **say-do gap**: stated purchase intent reliably overstates real purchasing, especially about price and about virtuous behavior. "Would you pay $30 a month for this?" is nearly worthless. "What are you paying today, and what did you do the last time you needed this?" is not.
segments.tr: 2. *Was Sie gefragt haben.* Achten Sie auf **führende** Fragen ("Wie sehr haben Sie unseren neuen Checkout genossen?"), **Doppelfragen** ("Ist unser Checkout schnell und einfach?" — welche Hälfte beantworten Sie?), und **soziale Erwünschtheitsverzerrung**, bei der Menschen die schmeichelhafte Antwort geben. Dann gibt es noch die **Sag-Tu-Lücke**: Angegeben Kaufabsicht überschätzt zuverlässig echte Käufe, besonders bei Preis und tugenhaftem Verhalten. "Würde ich $30 pro Monat dafür zahlen?" ist fast wertlos. "Was zahlen Sie heute, und was haben Sie das letzte Mal getan, als Sie dies brauchten?" ist es nicht.

segments.src: **Half two: how buyers actually decide.** The standard model has five stages:
segments.tr: **Teil zwei: wie Käufer tatsächlich entscheiden.** Das Standardmodell hat fünf Stufen:

segments.src: 1. **Problem recognition** — a gap opens between where you are and where you want to be.
segments.tr: 1. **Problemanerkennung** — eine Lücke öffnet sich zwischen wo Sie sind und wo Sie sein möchten.

segments.src: 2. **Information search** — internal (memory) first, then external (reviews, friends, retail floors).
segments.tr: 2. **Informationssuche** — intern (Gedächtnis) zuerst, dann extern (Rezensionen, Freunde, im Geschäft).

segments.src: 3. **Evaluation of alternatives** — a short **consideration set** gets scored on a handful of **evaluative criteria**.
segments.tr: 3. **Bewertung von Alternativen** — eine kleine **Betrachtungsmenge** wird anhand weniger **Bewertungskriterien** bewertet.

segments.src: 4. **Purchase decision** — plus the last-second friction that kills it: shipping cost, out of stock, a bad checkout.
segments.tr: 4. **Kaufentscheidung** — plus die Reibung in der letzten Sekunde, die es zunichte macht: Versandkosten, ausverkauft, ein schlechter Checkout.

segments.src: 5. **Post-purchase behavior** — satisfaction, **post-purchase dissonance** (buyer's remorse), returns, reviews, repeat business.
segments.tr: 5. **Verhalten nach dem Kauf** — Zufriedenheit, **Dissonanz nach dem Kauf** (Kaufreue), Rückgaben, Bewertungen, Wiederholungsgeschäfte.

segments.src: Not every purchase runs the full loop.
segments.tr: Nicht jeder Kauf läuft die volle Schleife ab.

segments.src: **High-involvement** buys — expensive, risky, identity-relevant — get the extended treatment.
segments.tr: **High-Involvement**-Käufe — teuer, riskant, identitätsrelevant — erhalten die erweiterte Behandlung.

segments.src: Low-involvement ones (toothpaste, gas station coffee) are mostly habit, which is why for those categories the real battleground is availability and cue, not persuasion.
segments.tr: Low-Involvement-Käufe (Zahnpasta, Tankstellen-Kaffee) sind meistens Gewohnheit, weshalb in diesen Kategorien das wirkliche Schlachtfeld Verfügbarkeit und Hinweis, nicht Überzeugung ist.

segments.src: Put the halves together and you get the useful rule: **choose your research design based on the stage where you're losing people.**
segments.tr: Fügen Sie die Hälften zusammen und Sie erhalten die nützliche Regel: **wählen Sie Ihr Forschungsdesign basierend auf der Phase, in der Sie Menschen verlieren.**

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Maya moves into a one-bedroom in Denver and, on night three, wakes up with her lower back aching.
segments.tr: Maya zieht in ein Ein-Zimmer-Apartment in Denver und wacht in der dritten Nacht mit Rückenschmerzen auf.

segments.src: That's **problem recognition** — nothing about her mattress changed, but her tolerance did.
segments.tr: Das ist **Problemanerkennung** — nichts an ihrer Matratze hat sich geändert, aber ihre Toleranz.

segments.src: **Information search:** she texts two friends, reads a "best mattress 2026" roundup, watches a YouTube teardown, and — because she's spending real money — drives to a store on Colorado Boulevard to lie on three of them for ninety seconds each.
segments.tr: **Informationssuche:** Sie textet zwei Freunde, liest einen "beste Matratze 2026"-Roundup, schaut sich einen YouTube-Teardown an, und — weil sie echtes Geld ausgibt — fährt zu einem Geschäft in der Colorado Boulevard, um auf drei von ihnen für jeweils neunzig Sekunden zu liegen.

segments.src: **Evaluation of alternatives:** her **consideration set** narrows to three brands.
segments.tr: **Bewertung von Alternativen:** ihre **Betrachtungsmenge** verengt sich auf drei Marken.

segments.src: Her **evaluative criteria** turn out to be firmness, a sleep trial she can actually use, and price under about $1,500.
segments.tr: Ihre **Bewertungskriterien** sind Festigkeit, eine Schlafprobe, die sie tatsächlich nutzen kann, und ein Preis von etwa unter $1,500.

segments.src: Note that "made in the USA" was in the ad that got her attention but never made her criteria list — attention and criteria are different things.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie, dass "hergestellt in den USA" in der Anzeige war, die ihre Aufmerksamkeit erregte, aber nie auf ihre Kriterienliste kam — Aufmerksamkeit und Kriterien sind unterschiedliche Dinge.

segments.src: **Purchase decision:** she picks a $1,400 queen at 11 p.m., then almost bails when old-mattress removal costs $99 extra.
segments.tr: **Kaufentscheidung:** Sie wählt eine $1,400-Queen um 23 Uhr, dann bricht fast ab, wenn die Altmatratzenentfernung $99 extra kostet.

segments.src: Free removal in the cart is what closes it.
segments.tr: Kostenlose Entfernung im Warenkorb ist das, was es schließt.

segments.src: **Post-purchase:** week one is rough.
segments.tr: **Nach dem Kauf:** Die erste Woche ist hart.

segments.src: She rereads the reviews she already read, looking for someone saying "it takes two weeks to adjust."
segments.tr: Sie liest die Rezensionen, die sie bereits gelesen hat, erneut durch und sucht nach jemandem, der sagt "es dauert zwei Wochen, sich anzupassen."

segments.src: That's **post-purchase dissonance**, and it's the moment brands either earn a five-star review or a return.
segments.tr: Das ist **Dissonanz nach dem Kauf**, und es ist der Moment, in dem Marken entweder eine Fünf-Sterne-Bewertung oder eine Rückgabe verdienen.

segments.src: Now flip to the mattress company's side.
segments.tr: Jetzt zur Seite des Matratzenherstellers.

segments.src: If Maya's story is typical, the research plan writes itself, stage by stage:
segments.tr: Wenn Mayas Geschichte typisch ist, schreibt sich der Forschungsplan selbst, Phase für Phase:

segments.src: - Suspect people don't know what firmness they need? That's fuzzy — run **exploratory** interviews with recent buyers.
segments.tr: - Vermuten Sie, dass Menschen nicht wissen, welche Festigkeit sie benötigen? Das ist verschwommen — führen Sie **explorative** Interviews mit kürzlichen Käufern durch.

segments.src: - Want to know what share of buyers rank a sleep trial above price? That's a count — run a **descriptive** survey on a probability sample of the customer list, and chase non-responders so it isn't just the enthusiasts.
segments.tr: - Möchten Sie wissen, welcher Anteil der Käufer eine Schlafprobe höher bewertet als den Preis? Das ist eine Zählung — führen Sie eine **deskriptive** Umfrage auf einer Wahrscheinlichkeitsstichprobe der Kundenliste durch und verfolgen Sie Nicht-Responder, damit es nicht nur die Enthusiasten sind.

segments.src: - Think free removal lifts conversion? Don't survey it — people are terrible at reporting what a $99 fee does to them. Run a **causal** A/B test at checkout and watch behavior.
segments.tr: - Denken Sie, dass kostenlose Entfernung die Konversion erhöht? Befragen Sie das nicht — Menschen sind schrecklich darin, zu berichten, was eine $99-Gebühr mit ihnen macht. Führen Sie einen **kausalen** A/B-Test beim Checkout durch und beobachten Sie das Verhalten.

segments.src: - Worried about returns in week two? That's a post-purchase problem, and the fix is probably an email on day 5 explaining the adjustment period, not a better ad.
segments.tr: - Sorge um Rückgaben in Woche zwei? Das ist ein Problem nach dem Kauf, und die Lösung ist wahrscheinlich eine E-Mail am Tag 5, die die Anpassungszeit erklärt, nicht eine bessere Anzeige.

segments.src: Same company, four questions, four different designs.
segments.tr: Gleiches Unternehmen, vier Fragen, vier verschiedene Designs.

segments.src: A single "customer satisfaction survey" would have answered none of them well.
segments.tr: Eine einzelne "Kundenzufriedenheitsumfrage" würde keiner von ihnen gut beantwortet haben.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Match the design to the question: exploratory to find hypotheses, descriptive to measure them, causal to prove what drives what — and check secondary data before you spend a dollar on primary.
segments.tr: 1. Passen Sie das Design zur Frage: explorative Forschung um Hypothesen zu finden, deskriptive um sie zu messen, kausal um zu beweisen, was was treibt — und prüfen Sie Sekundärdaten, bevor Sie einen Dollar auf Primärdaten ausgeben.

segments.src: 2. A survey is only as good as who answered and how you asked; non-response bias, leading or double-barreled wording, and the say-do gap ruin more studies than small sample sizes do.
segments.tr: 2. Eine Umfrage ist nur so gut wie wer antwortet und wie Sie fragen; Nichtantwort-Verzerrung, führende oder Doppel-Wording und die Sag-Tu-Lücke ruinieren mehr Studien als kleine Stichprobengrößen.

segments.src: 3. Buyers move through problem recognition → search → evaluation → purchase → post-purchase, and the stage where you're losing them tells you which research to run.
segments.tr: 3. Käufer bewegen sich durch Problemanerkennung → Suche → Bewertung → Kauf → Nach dem Kauf, und die Phase, in der Sie sie verlieren, zeigt Ihnen, welche Forschung Sie durchführen sollten.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbstquiz

segments.src: **1.** A direct-to-consumer coffee brand wants to know whether a $5-off coupon actually causes repeat orders, or whether the people who redeem it would have reordered anyway.
segments.tr: **1.** Eine Direct-to-Consumer-Kaffee-Marke möchte wissen, ob ein $5-Rabatt-Gutschein tatsächlich Wiederbestellungen verursacht, oder ob die Menschen, die ihn einlösen, sowieso wieder bestellen würden.

segments.src: Which research design fits?
segments.tr: Welches Forschungsdesign passt?

segments.src: - A. Exploratory — run two focus groups about coupons
segments.tr: - A. Explorative — zwei Fokusgruppen über Gutscheine durchführen

segments.src: - B. Descriptive — survey customers on how much they like coupons
segments.tr: - B. Deskriptiv — Kunden befragen, wie viel ihnen Gutscheine gefallen

segments.src: - C. Causal — randomly give the coupon to one group, withhold it from a comparable group, compare reorder rates
segments.tr: - C. Kausal — geben Sie den Gutschein zufällig einer Gruppe, behalten Sie ihn von einer vergleichbaren Gruppe vor, vergleichen Sie die Wiederbestellungsquoten

segments.src: - D. Secondary — buy an industry report on coupon usage
segments.tr: - D. Sekundär — einen Branchenbericht über Gutscheinnutzung kaufen

segments.src: **2.** True or False: "Is our checkout fast and easy?"
segments.tr: **2.** Wahr oder Falsch: "Ist unser Checkout schnell und einfach?"

segments.src: is a well-written survey question.

segments.tr: **3.** Ein Käufer, der bereits $1,400 bezahlt hat, liest die Rezensionen immer wieder durch, um sich selbst zu versichern, dass sie die richtige Wahl getroffen hat.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Heutige Begriffe

segments.src: - **Secondary data** — information collected by someone else for another purpose (Census tables, trade reports, your own past sales); cheap and fast, but rarely a perfect fit for your question.
segments.tr: - **Sekundärdaten** — Informationen, die von jemand anderen für einen anderen Zweck gesammelt wurden (Census-Tabellen, Branchenberichte, Ihre eigenen früheren Verkäufe); billig und schnell, aber selten perfekt für Ihre Frage.

segments.src: - **Probability sample** — a sample in which every member of the sampling frame has a known, non-zero chance of being selected; the precondition that makes margin of error meaningful.
segments.tr: - **Wahrscheinlichkeitsstichprobe** — eine Stichprobe, bei der jedes Mitglied des Stichprobenrahmens eine bekannte, nicht-null Auswahlwahrscheinlichkeit hat; die Vorbedingung, die die Fehlermarge aussagekräftig macht.

segments.src: - **Non-response bias** — distortion that occurs when the people who don't answer differ systematically from those who do; more responses don't fix it.
segments.tr: - **Nichtantwort-Verzerrung** — Verzerrung, die auftritt, wenn sich die Menschen, die nicht antworten, systematisch von denen unterscheiden, die es tun; mehr Antworten beheben es nicht.

segments.src: - **Consideration set** — the small handful of brands a buyer actually weighs at the evaluation stage; being known but not in the set is a distinct problem from being unknown.
segments.tr: - **Betrachtungsmenge** — die kleine Handvoll Marken, die ein Käufer tatsächlich in der Bewertungsphase abwägt; bekannt zu sein, aber nicht in der Menge, ist ein anderes Problem als unbekannt zu sein.

segments.src: - **Post-purchase dissonance** — the doubt a buyer feels after committing, especially on high-involvement purchases; managing it drives returns, reviews, and repeat business.
segments.tr: - **Dissonanz nach dem Kauf** — der Zweifel, den ein Käufer nach der Verpflichtung empfindet, besonders bei High-Involvement-Käufen; die Verwaltung davon treibt Rückgaben, Bewertungen und Wiederholungsgeschäfte.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — C.** Only a controlled experiment separates "the coupon caused the reorder" from "reorder-prone customers redeem coupons."
segments.tr: *Antworten: **1 — C.** Nur ein kontrolliertes Experiment trennt "der Gutschein verursachte die Wiederbestellung" von "wiederbestellungsanfällige Kunden lösen Gutscheine ein."

segments.src: A survey measures opinion about coupons, not their effect.
segments.tr: Eine Umfrage misst die Meinung über Gutscheine, nicht ihre Auswirkung.

segments.src: **2 — False.** It's double-barreled ("fast" and "easy" are two questions with possibly opposite answers) and leading.
segments.tr: **2 — Falsch.** Es ist doppelläufig ("schnell" und "einfach" sind zwei Fragen mit möglicherweise gegensätzlichen Antworten) und führend.

segments.src: Split it into two neutral items.
segments.tr: Teilen Sie es in zwei neutrale Elemente auf.

segments.src: **3 — D.** Rereading reviews after paying is post-purchase dissonance, not information search — the search is over; she's now reducing doubt about a decision already made.*
segments.tr: **3 — D.** Das Lesen von Rezensionen nach dem Bezahlen ist Dissonanz nach dem Kauf, keine Informationssuche — die Suche ist vorbei; sie reduziert jetzt Zweifel an einer bereits getroffenen Entscheidung.*
